Sports.title: "Same as Brazil" – Red Bull "trying to understand" the root cause of Verstappen's complaints
Sports.content:
After Thursday's practice sessions in Las Vegas, Red Bull – like all Formula 1 teams – has been left with very few answers. Isack Hadjar eventually finished fourth on the timesheets, but that means very little given that no more rain is forecast for the remainder of the weekend.

The conditions were therefore not representative during the practice day, and that was precisely why Max Verstappen stayed in the garage for so long. It was only in the final five minutes, following the late red flag, that the Dutchman set his first timed lap. There was simply very little to learn.

Read Also: Formula 1 What we learned from Thursday practice at the 2026 Las Vegas GP

Nevertheless, Verstappen was not happy with the RB22 during his brief appearance on track.

It started with a suspected power unit issue, with Verstappen reporting a lack of power on his out-lap. Red Bull responded by explaining that it was mainly related to the low temperatures and would improve on its own, although Verstappen replied: "This is not normal!"

After the session, technical director Pierre Wache explained the background to these complaints, which were also heard from Verstappen's team-mate Hadjar.

"I think it's mainly energy management and the MGU-K deployment around the lap. There was a little bit of fine-tuning on that aspect to make sure that it's optimised for the lap," Wache said.

"When the grip is so low in these conditions, the adaptation of the energy management takes some time on our side."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

However, that was not Verstappen's only complaint. The four-time world champion also said over the team radio: "This car is not good guys, same problem as Brazil."

Wache stressed that this was not related to the DM01 power unit, nor to engine braking – another aspect that has frequently troubled Verstappen this year – but purely to the car's balance.

"No, that's not about the power unit. It’s about the car balance, he was not happy with how the car behaved. We are trying to understand where it's coming from."

In Sao Paulo, Verstappen said that the balance had changed completely after the first stint on intermediates. According to him, this could not be fully explained by the switch to slick tyres, as the car also felt very different during the final laps on inters compared to the opening phase.

During practice in Las Vegas, Verstappen experienced the same balance problems at the rear of the car, something Red Bull will look into ahead of qualifying.

Nevertheless, Hadjar said he has "a good feeling" about this street circuit, although Wache is not yet prepared to fully share that optimism.

"I'm never optimistic. We have a lot of work to do, but it's unknown where we are," he said. "I think everybody is bringing some kind of update. Some teams are even bringing some engine updates.

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Manuel Eletto

"We will see where we are. It's difficult to say. At the moment, Max is not very happy with the car, and Isack is. We have to work on it and see how we can extrapolate it to tomorrow’s conditions."

While Wache mentioned upgrades, Red Bull has also brought a minor update to the Nevada desert. It involves a small modification to the front wing endplate, which Hadjar has said is worth "less than a tenth".

However, due to the tricky conditions, Red Bull has not yet been able to test the new part and will have to wait until the third practice session to do so.

Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell fastest in damp FP2 from Gasly
Sports.content:
George Russell pipped Pierre Gasly to go fastest in second practice for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix thanks to a late time in slippery conditions.

The Mercedes driver set a 1m47.272s at the chequered flag which put him 0.071s ahead of Gasly, who benefitted from track evolution to take a shock second for Alpine.

This was the first relatively meaningful session of the weekend after a rain-disrupted FP1 caused zero lap times to be set in the cold conditions - as low as 11C in FP2.

So it still caused complications, especially with the damp track, as drivers went out early on wets but Oscar Piastri quickly called for intermediates - despite McLaren’s insistence for the blue-striped rubber, which was initially correct.

Piastri set a 2m02.786s with his first lap, 3.256s slower than team-mate Lando Norris (1m59.530s) who set the pace in the opening few minutes as Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc split the pair after a 2m02.482s.

But these lap times were only temporary with track evolution being significant in Vegas, as Leclerc and Piastri greeted the top in the following minutes while battling the slippery conditions.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Manuel Eletto

It saw Max Verstappen go deep at Turn 7, likewise for Nico Hulkenberg at Turn 12, nearly colliding with Leclerc at the corner exit, while Norris also ventured off at Turn 14 during the opening 20 minutes.

By the end of that Leclerc was top with a 1m54.895s, 0.538s quicker than team-mate Lewis Hamilton, while Piastri (+0.574s), Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar (+0.881s) and Norris (+0.947s) completed the top five.

Then came the time for intermediates, however, as Norris went fastest with a 1m54.615s on his first run using that rubber, going two seconds quicker on his next lap by setting a 1m52.432s.

The 2025 champion had lowered that to a 1m50.930s by the halfway point, soon beaten by Leclerc and Hamilton who respectively achieved a 1m49.166s and 1m49.262s.

Those were set while heading into the final 20 minutes, just as Leclerc pitched for slick rubber, though Ferrari shot this down with the second half of a lap still proving too damp and slippery.

Both Rafael Camara and Gabriel Bortoleto, for example, went off at Turn 12, but track evolution was still prevalent as Leclerc improved to a 1m47.605s, 0.802s quicker than second-placed Hadjar.

A brief red flag threatened to end proceedings with 10 minutes left, due to a piece of plastic on track which Lance Stroll ran over, before the pitlane reopened for the final five minutes.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Manuel Eletto

There was still debate over whether to stick to the inters, a question Mercedes indirectly posed to Russell who jokingly responded, “if you’re asking about slicks, no way Jose!”

So all drivers stuck to the intermediate tyres, while it was Red Bull’s misery initially dominated discussion, as Verstappen reported power problems to struggle to a 1m50.141s for his only lap time of FP2.

Hadjar, meanwhile, had gone purple in the first two sectors until frustratingly being held up by Oliver Bearman during the final four corners, complaining “what he just did is crazy”.

But some drivers still managed to improve as Russell darted to the top with his 1m47.272s, while Gasly rose to second by setting a 1m47.343s at the chequered flag.

It meant Leclerc dropped to third on his 1m47.605s, ahead of fourth-placed Hadjar, while Piastri completed the top five and was 1.181s off Russell whose ex-team-mate Hamilton took sixth.

Norris (+1.565s), 2026 champion Kimi Antonelli (+1.771s), Franco Colapinto (+1.957s) and Fernando Alonso (+1.959s) round out the top 10, with Verstappen down in 13th.

Sports.title: Cadillac ditches plan to produce own V6 hybrid engine ahead of F1’s V8 push
Sports.content:
Cadillac is set to delay the introduction of its in-house Formula 1 power unit by a year to 2030.

The American squad's initial plan was to compete in the championship with its own General Motors power unit for the first time in 2029. However, that was based on the idea that the current regulations cycle would run its full course and that the next generation of power units would not be introduced until 2031.

That situation has since changed. Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the teams and manufacturers reached an agreement in principle on bringing forward the return of V8 engines, as the McLaren CEO Zak Brown also publicly confirmed during the team principals' press conference on Thursday.

The signatures have not yet been put on paper, as Alpine team principal Flavio Briatore added, but an agreement has been reached on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a reduced proportion of electrical power from 2030.

This development has implications for General Motors' plans. If the American manufacturer were to press ahead with its intention to turn Cadillac into a works team as early as 2029, GM would have to develop a power unit to the current specifications for just a single season. That would be a costly undertaking.

Asked by Autosport whether it would therefore make more sense to continue as a customer team for an extra season, CEO Dan Towriss confirmed in Las Vegas: "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8."

Dan Towriss, Cadillac Racing Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Towriss sees the arrival of the V8 as a positive development for F1, and one that Cadillac supports.

"Yeah, I mean, I think we're glad to see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030. We're super happy with that," Towriss said.

He added that Cadillac and General Motors are approaching another milestone. In less than a month's time, their dedicated power unit facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, will open.

"Yes, our new power unit facility opens up on December 18," he said. "So as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, having this direction is obviously very helpful. We're excited about the direction and the crew's hard at work getting ready."

Besides being expected to appeal more to fans, the V8 is also intended to be simpler and cheaper, which is likewise good news for a newcomer.

When the facility begins operations, Cadillac will initially still be working on both V6 and V8 designs, although the current generation of power units will no longer need to be fully developed for 2029.

"Well, for a period of time, we're working on both. So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we’re working towards the V8," Towriss explained.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

"There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in."

This should lead to the introduction of Cadillac's first in-house power unit in 2030, officially making the American newcomer a works team. That long-term ambition was also important in securing approval for its F1 entry, as the other teams saw it as the main source of added value for F1 as a whole.

Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Rain drowns out FP1
Sports.content:
"If we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble," Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson predicted after sampling this year's rain tyres in Brazil.

His comments reflected the general mood in the paddock as the Pirelli tyres are difficult to bring up to temperature, especially at a circuit with low corner speeds and glacial temperatures like the 6km street circuit in the gambling haven.

Lawson's comments proved relevant as the heavens opened up intermittently in Nevada on Thursday morning, and more rain arrived right before the start of FP1 at 4:30 pm local time.

With little rain expected for the remainder of the weekend, it naturally led to an action-starved session, leaving fans forking out the event's eye-watering ticket prices to look for action at the blackjack tables instead.

Venturing out on the low-grip surface, with the walls looming large, felt like a gamble, too. But as if intent to at least offer the home fans something, Sergio Perez of US-owned team Cadillac was first to brave the conditions on full wet tyres for an exploratory lap. He was later joined by Haas duo Rafael Camara and Ryo Hirakawa, the latter completing a rookie FP1 session instead of Oliver Bearman.

The second Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas also explored the inclement conditions, celebrating his 2027 confirmation with a huge tank slapper on his one lap, showing the two US-owned teams certainly couldn't be accused of not chipping in.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

While TV audiences and punters intent on analysing lap times and long runs were also left wanting, FP1 actually became one of the most picturesque sessions of the year. The Las Vegas Boulevard is photogenic at the best of times, but the rain further drowned the Strip in neon-tinted reflections, hues Hunter S. Thompson would have approved of.

"Amazing, it's a lovely Strip," gawked Ferrari reserve driver Dino Beganovic as he replaced Lewis Hamilton for the session.

"Enjoy the sightseeing... but we'll box this lap, please," came the perfunctory reply from Ferrari.

Beganovic may as well have enjoyed it, as staying tucking inside the garage was not an option to begin with for the Swedish-Bosnian driver. For any of the teams' four mandatory rookie FP1 sessions to count, drivers must at least leave the garage once.

It explains why all three rookie runners went out, including Jak Crawford who deputised for Fernando Alonso at Aston Martin, though they will be ruing the lack of actual mileage the rare opportunity was able to provide.

As world champion Kimi Antonelli reported aquaplaning, several more tenured drivers had close shaves with the walls. Alex Albon went straight at Turn 11 at the end of the Strip , while Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also locked up at the drenched left-hander.

"It's almost like an ice rink," reported Red Bull's Max Verstappen, The Dutchman a rather cool admirer of street circuits at the best of times.

Eventually, all but five drivers sampled the conditions, with the four cars from McLaren and Racing Bulls thinking better of it, and Aston's Lance Stroll also not feeling particularly motivated.

Camara and Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto were the only three drivers to venture out twice, with the Argentine nearly reliving the scenes of his high-speed qualifying shunt in 2024 for Williams as he momentarily lost control over his car on the straight.

For the avoidance of doubt, no laptimes were recorded.

Sports.title: Nike joins F1 as apparel partner
Sports.content:
Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027.

As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear from the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

The athletic company will also come up with F1-inspired retail collections, the first of which will go on sale on Friday and be centred around the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

"Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans," the announcement promised.

"Fans will get a first look on 20 November, when the limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection drops at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill said: "Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

Sports.title: FIA to phase in full-time F1 stewards from 2027
Sports.content:
The consistency of stewards’ decisions has been a topic of discussion in the Formula 1 paddock for years. While the complexity of the sporting regulations and racing guidelines is one factor, another question keeps coming up: would a permanent panel of stewards improve consistency?

From 2027, the FIA will take a step in that direction. The governing body announced on Thursday that it will gradually move towards full-time stewards, with the first phase beginning in 2027.

The intention is to recruit a panel of 12 to 15 full-time stewards, although that number will only be reached over time. The first full-time stewards will be recruited during the 2027 season, who will be joined at each race by the usual part-time stewards and a driver’s steward, whose specialist knowledge and perspective as a former racing driver will remain part of the process.

The main objective is to improve the consistency of decisions, although according to the FIA, the initiative goes beyond that. By making the role full-time, these stewards can also be deployed outside race weekends, for example “to identify emerging trends and areas requiring regulatory clarification” and to train FIA officials.

That would allow for shortcomings in the sporting regulations and racing guidelines used by stewards to be addressed more effectively. The aim is therefore not only to improve consistency during races, but also to make the rules and guidelines themselves more robust in the first place.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

This move is in line with what FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been advocating for some time: further professionalisation of the stewarding panel. The FIA believes moving beyond the current voluntary, rotating system will help improve continuity and consistency.

And that is precisely one of the key areas the FIA wants to improve, while emphasising that the move also complements the FIA Remote Operations Centre, which recently opened at Biggin Hill.

“This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport,” Ben Sulayem said.

“This development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships.”

The FIA is now setting up the recruitment process for the phased introduction in 2027, with plans to expand the group in 2028 and subsequent years until it reaches the target of 12 to 15 full-time stewards.

Sports.title: Hamilton insists there are no "trust" problems at Ferrari
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has insisted there are zero “trust” problems at Ferrari despite him overruling strategic calls becoming a repeated occurrence across recent Formula 1 grands prix.

The seven-time world champion has ignored calls to pit in two of the last four rounds - Singapore and Brazil - with both backfiring on the Scuderia driver.

In Singapore he elected to keep track position under a virtual safety car, but on worn tyres he dropped from podium contention to sixth late on - for which he apologised afterwards.

Then in Brazil last time out, Hamilton stayed on slicks despite the rain intensifying and this led to a late spin at the final corner before pitting the following lap to eventually finish ninth.

Those instances came amid talk of fractious relations down at Ferrari but ahead of this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed all is well - particularly with his new-for-2026 race engineer Carlo Santi.

“It’s definitely not a trust thing, we’re constantly working on our communication,” said the 41-year-old.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"It's been a lot better this year. Carlo has done an amazing job and those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed.

“I got the call right at the last minute. We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction."

This year has been much improved for Hamilton, who is fourth in the standings with three rounds remaining, currently on 261 points compared to his total of 156 in 2025.

His first year in Ferrari colours was certainly underwhelming, but there have still been signs of improvement in 2026 despite it being a significant jump from last season.

Not only is that in reference to the strategic calls, but also his connection with team-mate Charles Leclerc, clashing on a few occasions and most notably in Mexico three weeks ago.

It cost Ferrari the win and Hamilton subsequently criticised Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude, before suggesting in Sao Paulo that the Monegasque races him harder than he does with other drivers.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Yuri Cortez / AFP via Getty Images

That led to an hour-long meeting between both Scuderia drivers plus team boss Fred Vasseur and Hamilton and Leclerc are now confident that the issue has been resolved.

“Charles is a great driver,” said Hamilton. “The detail we went into about stuff like that, in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear, we understand each other, we understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.

“So I don't feel like that will be a problem moving forward. I have no concerns or worries about racing him, and I don't think he does for me either.”

The talk surrounding the Mexico clash was naturally high, but Leclerc reckons that is a consequence of driving for Ferrari and all focus is now on securing runner-up in the constructors’ standings.

“Everything has been taken out of proportion,” said Leclerc. “I'm kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years. But things are very often taken out of proportion.

“The goal is not always to agree and that will never happen. We can have different opinions and that was the case, for example, in Mexico.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

“But just the fact of speaking eased all tensions and we were completely fine with it. It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time.

“We started speaking about many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward.

“But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes and then the air was clean and that's it.”

Ferrari heads into the Vegas race 95 points ahead of third-placed Red Bull and 142 behind Mercedes, who clinched its ninth title at Interlagos.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Report claims Stellantis will cancel its Peugeot WEC and Citroen Formula E programmes | Brief
Sports.content:
Car manufacturer Stellantis is preparing to cancel its motorsport programmes according to media reports in France.

Le Figaro claims the manufacturer, whose brands include Peugeot and Citroen, will announce the decision next week.

Peugeot finished seventh in the World Endurance Championship this year, for the second season in a row. It has not won a race since returning to the championship with its unconventional 9X8 design in 2022.

Citroen’s Formula E team came fifth in the standings last year with drivers Jean-Eric Vergne and Nick Cassidy. The latter scored their only win of the season, in Mexico.

Sports.title: “He’s decided on a direction”: Cadillac offered reserve role to “disappointed” Herta | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has offered Colton Herta a reserve driver role for next season after choosing not to promote him to a race seat for 2027.

The IndyCar race-winner competed in Formula 2 this year to prepare himself for a potential Formula 1 debut in 2027. He has endured a tough campaign and lies 19th in the standings after 25 out of 29 races.

Herta secured enough FIA superlicence points to race in F1 through his appearances for Cadillac in practice sessions. Despite this, Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss said the team felt it would be best to retain its current line-up.

“We were working hard to get Colton Herta ready as well,” he said. “It’s important to have an American driver with our team racing.

“But ultimately, when we took a look at it, Valtteri is the right guy. We want to keep Checo and Valtteri together. Their experience, the continuity, what they bring to the team, ultimately it was the right decision for the team and we were happy to extend Valtteri. He’s been absolutely fantastic for us.”

Herta has “a number of options on the table” for 2027. “We’ve offered him a reserve position. The seat’s open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton.

“There are options in other sports as well. I think he’s decided on a direction, but we’re still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.”

Towriss said it had been “a tough decision [and] tough discussion with Colton” about his future. “I think he was disappointed.

“There was a lot of work, a lot of build-up going to this. I think Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in.

“I think it was obvious it was a very tough season for Colton in F2 this year, but I think the work that he did in FP1s and the testing [of previous cars] were quite strong and showed that he really is capable of driving this car.

“But when we look at where the team is right now and what’s needed for the team, Valtteri was the best decision going forward. But again, we’re going to continue to talk to Colton about the options that are on the table and give it a little bit of time, because I think he is disappointed to not have that opportunity.

“So much went into this, but he’s just a tremendous talent, and we’re excited about what’s ahead for him.”

Sports.title: Las Vegas F1 track is “not made for these conditions” – Bearman | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman says the rain which made driving impossible in Las Vegas today wouldn’t have been a problem at other tracks.

No drivers set any lap times during the first practice session at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit due to the wet conditions. Only 17 of the 22 cars took to the track and none of them completed more than two laps during the 60-minute session.

Bearman said a similar volume of rain would have been less of a problem at a track such as Interlagos, which was hit by rain when F1 visited it two weeks ago.

“This track is not made for these conditions,” said Bearman. “It’s incredibly cold this time of year. The track is also very, very smooth, so the smallest amount of water is enough to cause a lot of aquaplaning, because the water really sits on top.

“We have a lot of other tracks where, when it rains, the grip is actually still there. At turn 12 there’s huge puddles and even in the straights as well the water takes a long time to go away.

“So if that was Brazil last week that amount of rain we would be running in FP1 but in this track it’s impossible especially with those low temps with the tyres we have this year. So it’s a real recipe for disaster.”

Bearman was not due to participate in first practice as Haas test driver Ryo Hirakawa took over his car. “I missed FP1 anyway, but everybody did, so it’s not the end of the world,” said Bearman.

“Even in FP2 at the end 90% of the circuit is dry and on any other track you would fit the slick and go much, much quicker, but there was no chance of it here because the grip is so low.”

Hirakawa admitted the grip at the track was even lower than he expected. “It was quite tricky,” he said. “I knew that the track was going to be very slippery, but it was even worse than I thought.

“There was no grip and I just wanted to complete all the check-ups [to see] that the car was working. I took margin, but there was no grip out there.”

Sports.title: Wet Las Vegas practice was like a cold, miserable day karting at Rowrah – Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton said the rain-hit practice session at Las Vegas reminded him of his early days karting in the north of England.

The Ferrari driver did not take part in the first practice session, when no driver set a time as the track was soaked.

“It wasn’t really a great day, just sitting around waiting,” said Hamilton. “I didn’t do much today.

“You can’t really test much in those conditions. Everything you learn from today you have to kind of forget because tomorrow is supposed to be dry. So we’ll start from tomorrow.”

The conditions improved in time for second practice when Hamilton covered 26 laps and set the sixth-fastest time. The track began to dry out towards the end of the session when drivers switched to intermediate tyres, which Hamilton said allowed the team to gain some useful information.

“It’s just one of those days, it reminds me of an old day at like Rowrah in karting where it’s cold and miserable,” he said.

“But we didn’t really lose out much missing P1 because it was so wet, which was good. And then at least we got some running, there was a couple of good findings in the session as it goes from the wet to the inter so we got some learnings.”

Ferrari’s deputy team principal Jerome D’Ambrosio said they will attempt to cover as much of their incomplete running plan as they can during the final practice session tomorrow.

“We’re going to have to condense the long runs and the short runs for quali,” he said. “We’ll try to squeeze everything in in one hour, but we have no choice. It’s like this for everyone, and we’ll have to make the most out of it.”

Sports.title: F1 has “agreement in principle” to ditch 2026 engines after just four seasons | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team principals say they have agreed with the FIA to scrap the widely-criticised 2026 engine regulations ahead of schedule.

Team principals confirmed they have reached an agreement in principle to introduce a new formula in 2030. The previous engine regulations were used for 12 seasons from 2014 to 2025. The new agreement will see the current engines dropped after four years of use, having been in development for another four years prior to their introduction

The FIA has the power to impose new regulations of its own choosing in 2031. However it can introduce new rules earlier, in 2030, with the support of a sufficient majority of the engine manufacturers.

Team principals indicated the governing body has obtained the necessary support to introduce a new engine formula based on V8 engines. These are expected to retain turbochargers and use less powerful hybrid systems.

McLaren CEO Zak Brown said the teams reached an “agreement in principle” with the FIA. “I think now it’s about dotting the ‘i’s and crossing the ‘t’s”

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said earlier this week the new engines will arrive “soon”.

“We have the agreement, basically,” said Alpine executive consultant Flavio Briatore. “It’s not signed, but it looks like everybody’s agreed to 2030 V8s.”

The arrangement will force a change of plans for Cadillac, which currently uses Ferrari power units but had begun developing its own version of the current engines to introduce in 2029. CEO Dan Towriss said they will now extend their Ferrari deal by one year and start using their own engines in 2030.

“Our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th, so as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, the direction is obviously very helpful,” he said. “We’re excited about the direction, and the crew’s hard at work getting ready.”

“For a period of time, we were working on both [engine formulas],” he added. “So they’ve already got a V6 base to build off and [are] working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there’s a lot of good foundation for what we’re trying to build and the direction we’re headed in.”

Sports.title: Five drivers to take grid penalties at Las Vegas Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA has confirmed five drivers have exceeded their power unit parts allocation at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli , Oscar Piastri, Oliver Bearman, Carlos Sainz Jnr and Lance Stroll will all take grid penalties as a result.

Mercedes previously confirmed Antonelli will take a new engine and turbo this weekend, allowing him to use their new specification introduced under F1’s Additional Development Upgrade Opportunity regulations. George Russell will not do the same as he preferred to use the older specification and avoid a penalty.

As Antonelli has only exceeded the maximum number of power unit components with his new engine, which he has already replaced previously, he will take a five-place grid drop.

Two other Mercedes-powered drivers – Piastri at McLaren and Sainz at Williams – have exceeded their maximum allocation of components. They receive 10-place penalties.

Stroll will take his ninth new energy store and eighth new control electronics unit this year, putting the Honda driver even further beyond the maximum allocation of three each. He also receives a 10-place grid penalty.

Haas has fitted a complete new Ferrari power unit to Bearman’s car. He will therefore take a 35-place grid penalty, dropping him to the back of the grid.

Sports.title: Russell grabs fastest time after late red flag in second practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell led the second practice session on a drying track at Las Vegas, hitting the top of the times with his final lap.

After no drivers set a time in the soaked first session, water levels on the track remained high enough for full wet weather tyres as second practice began.

McLaren, Mercedes and Ferrari got down to work quickly, sending their drivers out for several laps. Lando Norris led the times to begin with, lapping the track in just under two minutes, around half a minute off dry weather times.

It took around 20 minutes for the track to dry sufficiently for drivers to be able to switch to intermediate tyres. Norris was one of the first to change, and despite sliding off at turn one, soon lowered the best time to a 1’50.930.

That stood as the fastest time as the session passed its halfway point, by which time some drivers still had not appeared, including Max Verstappen. Charles Leclerc eventually deposed Norris from the top of the times by producing a lap of 1’49.066.

Verstappen was finally preparing to join the track with around 10 minutes remaining when the session was red-flagged. Lance Stroll had encountered a large sheet of plastic approaching the fast turn 17, though fortunately it caused no serious harm.

When the session resumed with six minutes left, several drivers embarked on quick laps on intermediate tyres. Isack Hadjar was on course to beat Leclerc’s benchmark, setting the fastest time through the first two sectors, when he caught Oliver Bearman dawdling at turn 14. “Bearman is completely lost,” fumed Hadjar, “what he just did is crazy.”

Hadjar’s team mate was not happy either, complaining of a lack of power from his engine. “This is not normal,” he replied after his race engineer tried to reassure him. “This car is not good,” he added afterwards. “This is the same problem as Brazil.”

Russell eventually replaced Leclerc at the top of the times with a lap of 1’47.272. Pierre Gasly threatened it, setting the best time of anyone in the first sector, but fell shy by less than a tenth of a second.

Despite the challenging conditions, no one made significant contact with a barrier. Fernando Alonso touched one when he skidded wide at turn five, but avoided damaging his car. Gabriel Bortoleto also spun at turn 12.

Sports.title: Formula 1 teams set no lap times in wet first practice at Las Vegas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 fans at the Las Vegas circuit saw no meaningful action in the first practice session as teams avoided running on the extremely wet track.

The six-kilometre circuit was soaked before the session began. Most of the field – 17 of the 22 drivers – completed a single tour but none attempted to set a lap time. All of those who did appeared used the full wet weather tyre.

Sergio Perez, who remains yet to score a point this year, officially headed the times in his Cadillac as he was the first driver to join the track. With the Haas pair next and Valtteri Bottas following in the other Cadillac, the top four places were occupied by the American teams.

However with the risk of damage to the cars so high, some teams opted not to send their cars out at all. Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin never appeared, nor did either McLaren or Racing Bulls.

The disruption was especially disappointing for the three drivers who had been handed rare opportunities to appear in practice. Ryo Hirakawa was back in Oliver Bearman’s Haas, Aston martin ran Jak Crawford in Fernando Alonso’s car and Dino Beganovic took over Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari. All completed a single tour of the track and brought their cars back unscathced.

Franco Colapinto came closest to wrecking his car when his Alpine snapped sideways on the Strip. He caught the dramatic sideways moment before returning to the pits.

Max Verstappen summed up the conditions when he made his sole tour of the track in his Red Bull: “It’s like an ice rink.”

Sports.title: David Morrell Takes a Huge Step Backward Against Rodriguez
Sports.content:
David Morrell should beat Julio de Jesus Rodriguez on Saturday in Santo Domingo. The trouble is that even a quick knockout of the 44-year-old veteran will do little to repair the damage from Zak Chelli stopping him in the tenth round in May. For a fighter who was facing David Benavidez less than two years ago, this is a long way back.

Morrell (12-2, 9 KOs) is scheduled for ten rounds at light heavyweight against Rodriguez (27-10, 24 KOs) on Shuan Boxing’s card at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz. Rodriguez has knocked out 24 men, but he’s on a long losing streak and has been stopped by James Metcalf and Ismael Villarreal. At 28, Morrell should have the speed to get his punches off first and the power to end it early.

The Benavidez defeat was easier to take. Morrell went the distance in a competitive fight against one of the best men in the division. His split decision over Imam Khataev five months later was a harder result to read. He got the win, but it was close enough that he still had something to prove when he went to Manchester to fight Chelli. Getting stopped there took away the argument that he was only a step behind the very best.

Morrell has been out since May, and there’s value in getting him back in the ring. He can get his timing back, put combinations together, and see how comfortable he feels throwing the left hand. Rodriguez’s recent form makes an early finish the expectation. If Morrell struggles to put him away or has trouble keeping control of the fight, those questions about his form will follow him out of Santo Domingo.

The next opponent will tell us more. Morrell needs someone who can make him work into the later rounds and still bring something back at him. That’s where the Chelli loss leaves the biggest question, and Saturday’s opponent is unlikely to make Morrell answer it.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Claims Jai Opetaia Dodged Deontay Wilder Risk for Benavidez
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley is not buying the hand injury story that knocked Jai Opetaia out of his December 11 heavyweight fight against Deontay Wilder in Cardiff.

Bradley thinks the Australian cruiserweight and his team finally had a reality check about what happens when a smaller fighter steps up to take bombs from a natural heavyweight. Mick Francis of Tasman Fighters claimed Opetaia aggravated the hand in training while getting ready for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard, but Bradley says he needs to see actual proof before he believes it.

“I truly believe that Jai had a reality check, man, and really thought about what the hell he was doing, him and his team,” said Bradley on his channel.

Bradley is saying what every boxing fan already figured out the second the withdrawal news broke. Wilder might be past his prime, yet he still carries the kind of right hand that turns the lights out in a split second.

“All it takes for Deontay Wilder is one, and that’s it,” said Bradley.

As Bradley noted, Opetaia could have outboxed Wilder for ten rounds, only to get clipped with one clean shot and wake up looking at the arena lights. Had that happened, Benavidez already admitted he would have moved straight on to chasing Oleksandr Usyk instead.

Opetaia only took the Cardiff date because he stopped Noel Mikaelian in September and did not want to sit around until May waiting for Benavidez. Even if Opetaia had beaten Wilder, a cautious points win would have done nothing to build hype for the Benavidez fight.

Everything short of a highlight-reel knockout was a bad business move. Benavidez even admitted he was relieved when the Wilder fight fell apart. First, Benavidez has to get past Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona.

If Benavidez wins that unification bout and brings the WBA, WBC, and WBO belts to Las Vegas on Cinco de Mayo weekend, Opetaia gets his chance to win three world titles in one night.

Pulling out of the Wilder trap might look suspicious to Bradley, yet it easily saved Opetaia from ruining the biggest fight of his career.

Sports.title: Andy Hiraoka Signs With Zuffa, Moves to Welterweight
Sports.content:
Andy Hiraoka has signed a multi-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing and will move up to welterweight, the promotion announced. The Japanese southpaw enters the 147-pound division after pushing WBA light welterweight champion Gary Antuanne Russell hard enough in February to make a case that he deserved the decision.

Hiraoka (24-1, 19 KOs) went into that fight unbeaten and left with three scorecards that made Russell’s first title defense look comfortable. The Nevada commission recorded scores of 116-111 twice and 117-110 for Russell. Those margins were hard to square with what Hiraoka did in the second half, when he began hurting Russell to the body and forced the champion to give ground.

Russell had the better of the first five rounds in Las Vegas. He got his combinations off first and built a 60-36 edge in punches landed over that stretch, according to CompuBox. Hiraoka had landed only one body punch through five rounds. In the seventh alone, he landed 20. Once he started getting through downstairs, Russell had to spend more time fighting off his back foot.

Hiraoka landed 76 power punches to Russell’s 59 over the last six rounds. There were rounds in that stretch where Russell was still busy enough to give the judges a choice, but Hiraoka was landing the shots that changed how the fight was being fought. If you gave him one or two of the closer early rounds and most of the second half, you could get to a Hiraoka win. The point he lost for low blows in the 10th made his case harder, especially on a card where he was already giving away early rounds.

That fight against Russell put Hiraoka on the map in a way none of his domestic bouts in Japan ever could. Most guys who lose a decision on a big stage walk away with their stock dented, but Hiraoka actually raised his value because of how he broke Russell down in the second half.

You don’t often see a 140-pounder punish a champion to the ribs and liver like that, especially someone as physically strong as Russell. Watching Russell go from firing crisp combinations in the first five rounds to literally running out of room and looking desperate to survive down the stretch told the whole story. If not for that slow start and the point deduction in the 10th, Hiraoka walks out of Las Vegas with the WBA belt.

Before this signing, he was completely stuck in neutral. Fighting in Japan under Ohashi Promotions kept him off the radar for casual fans and made it almost impossible to lure top American or British names into the ring with him. Nobody wanted the risk for a low-profile payday.

“I feel like he was down on the scorecards and knew it, so he tried to pick up the intensity,” said Russell after the fight, as reported by The Ring. Hiraoka’s attack held up deep into the fight. He landed 13 power punches in the 12th, his second-highest total of the night, and finished just two behind Russell in power punches landed overall.

The move to 147 raises a question about how quickly Hiraoka can get that body attack going against bigger men. He found his way into the Russell fight by stepping close enough to hit the body after spending much of the opening rounds at a distance where Russell could get off first. A welterweight who can make him pay on the way in would put that adjustment to a different test.

Zuffa’s announcement named neither a debut date nor an opponent. The first opponent will tell us how much the promotion took from the Russell fight. A durable welterweight who can make Hiraoka work beyond the opening rounds would show whether the pressure he put on a champion at 140 comes with him to 147.

Sports.title: Senate Passes Ali Revival Act by Unanimous Consent
Sports.content:
The U.S. Senate passed the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act by unanimous consent Thursday, moving Zuffa Boxing’s league model a step closer to federal recognition. The bill would let leagues stage fights between boxers they sign and run their own title systems alongside the traditional sanctioning bodies.

The Senate Press Gallery confirmed that H.R. 4624 passed with a substitute amendment from Sens. Ted Cruz of Texas and Jacky Rosen of Nevada. The House, which passed an earlier version, must agree to the Senate’s changes before the bill can go to the president.

The bill’s biggest change is the creation of a legal path for Unified Boxing Organizations. Under the published Cruz–Rosen amendment, a league would match fighters under contract to it and could run its own rankings. It could also recognize titles and rankings from an independent organization. Fighters could choose to sign with a league or continue working with traditional promoters.

For Zuffa, the benefit is in the matchmaking. If two contenders are on the same roster, the league can put them together without first having to negotiate with a rival promoter. That could help keep a division moving when the best available opponents are already signed. The model is less helpful when the opponent fans want fights for somebody else. The league still needs enough depth in each division to make the fights it wants to sell.

For a boxer, the question is what happens when the league has the belt he wants and controls who gets the next shot. A contender can climb the rankings and still depend on the same company for a date, an opponent and a purse. The amendment addresses some of that leverage. It would generally cap promotional agreements at six years, limit a boxer’s first professional promotional agreement to three and allow talks with other promoters or leagues during the final 90 days of a deal. A boxer could sign a new agreement once the existing one expires.

The published amendment would also set a $200 minimum for each round a boxer participates in, covering traditional promoters as well as leagues. It would require at least $50,000 in medical coverage for injuries sustained during a bout and $15,000 in accidental death coverage. The leagues would also have to carry insurance for injuries sustained while training for a covered bout and use an independent third party to administer drug testing.

The test for Zuffa is whether it can sign enough contenders to make its belts worth chasing. A league can build a title fight from its own roster, but a belt is only as valuable as the competition behind it. For a fighter weighing a multi-year deal, the decisions that count are who he can fight, how often he gets booked and what he can earn by moving up.

Sports.title: De La Hoya Says WBA Cleared Teofimo Lopez for Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya says the WBA is giving Teofimo Lopez an exemption to fight Ryan Garcia before mandatory challenger Jack Catterall. The proposed February 6 welterweight unification could put Eddie Hearn’s threat to sue the WBA to the test if the association confirms that Lopez can keep his title and fight Garcia first.

“It has already been worked out,” said De La Hoya on Fight Hub TV when asked whether the Catterall mandatory could hold up the fight. “The WBA has already ruled on it. They’re giving an exemption to Teofimo Lopez because he is the world champion and this will be a unification.”

De La Hoya called it an exemption and gave no details of the ruling or its terms. The WBA’s November 11 public decision reaffirmed that Lopez must defend his Super title against Catterall and gave the camps 10 calendar days to reach an agreement or propose another solution. Either side could request a purse bid if talks failed.

The same decision said the WBA can consider a unification under its special permit rule. Mike Coppinger reported on November 14 that the WBA had informed the parties that Lopez could apply for a permit to face Garcia, the WBC champion. De La Hoya’s account goes a step further. He says the WBA has made its decision, though the association has yet to publicly confirm that it has granted an exemption.

“I would sue them immediately,” said Hearn on Inside the Ring last week when asked what he would do if the WBA ruled against him. The Matchroom promoter has argued that Catterall was already owed a shot at the Super title before Lopez took it from Rolando Romero. Catterall holds the WBA’s Regular belt and earned the right to challenge for the top title by beating Shakhram Giyasov.

If the WBA confirms De La Hoya’s account, the terms of the exemption could determine how long Catterall has to wait. A written ruling could spell out whether Catterall gets the winner and when that defense would be due. Hearn has been pressing for Catterall to get his shot first. If he follows through on his threat, the WBA’s November order and the terms of any exemption would both come into play.

De La Hoya said Las Vegas and New York were under consideration and that a few details remained to be worked out for February 6. He also said he had never spoken to Floyd Mayweather about making a fight with Garcia. Later in the interview, De La Hoya said he believed the Lopez deal was close. For Catterall, the immediate question is what the WBA will put in writing about the title shot it ordered.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Refuses To Admit Ryan Garcia Exposed His Style
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is still trying to convince fans he knows how to beat Ryan Garcia in a rematch, yet he refuses to admit what actually happened in their first fight. During his appearance on Club Shay Shay, Haney kept falling back on the same old excuse about Garcia’s left hook, calling them “PED punches.”

“It’s boxing. You get caught,” said Haney on Club Shay Shay. “But those PED punches … they were a little different.” Later, when asked whether he’d ever felt that kind of power in the division, he went right back to the positive drug test again.

Ostarine does not make a fighter drop his right hand every time he throws a jab. That was Haney’s biggest problem all night. He kept stepping forward behind his jab, ducking his head, and lunging in to clinch with his right glove down at his chest. Garcia saw that bad habit from a mile away and timed him with left hooks over the top. You do not need banned substances to hit a guy whose chin is sitting wide open.

Haney boasted about getting off the canvas three times, saying it proves he can take a punch. He also broke down what Conor Benn did wrong when Benn walked into Garcia’s shots. It is funny how Haney can spot another fighter’s mistakes from ringside, yet he still refuses to look in the mirror and fix his own. Until he admits his style is tailor-made for Garcia’s left hook, a rematch will end the exact same way.

Before Haney even thinks about fixing his mistakes for Garcia, he’s got to deal with IBF welterweight champ Liam Paro on December 19. You can tell Haney wants that Garcia rematch badly because the first fight wrecked his reputation with fans and killed his leverage at the negotiating table.

Looking past Paro is a massive mistake, though. If Haney loses that unification fight, he isn’t getting near a Garcia rematch anytime soon unless he’s willing to walk in coming off a loss, and you know the purse split would be totally against him in that spot.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Given WBC Green Light for Willy Hutchinson, Will Eddy Reynoso Block It?
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez has a clear path back to 175 pounds if he wants it. WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman told Sky Sports on Thursday that the sanctioning body would approve a fight between Canelo and WBC light heavyweight champion Willy Hutchinson as Hutchinson’s first title defense.

The WBC discussed Hutchinson’s mandatory status at its convention in Acapulco, but Sulaiman confirmed the organization left the division without an official ruling. Without a mandatory challenger ordered, the Scottish fighter could move directly from his November 7 decision win over Joshua Buatsi into a bout with Canelo.

The next move is with Canelo, who reclaimed the WBC super middleweight belt by outpointing Christian Mbilli on October 31.

“It would certainly be approved, champion against champion,” Sulaiman said to Sky Sports regarding a potential Canelo move back up to light heavyweight.

The real issue may not be the WBC, however, but trainer Eddy Reynoso. Once Reynoso scouts the Buatsi tape and sees Hutchinson’s length, lateral movement, and busy jab, he could easily decide the stylistic headache outweighs the reward of another belt at 175.

Moving up to face Hutchinson would certainly be courageous on Canelo’s part, yet there is a big difference between courage and plain common sense. Behind the scenes, it would be no surprise to see Reynoso steer Canelo toward safer, more lucrative waters at 168 against someone like Hamzah Sheeraz, defending his newly reclaimed title against a big UK draw rather than spending 12 frustrating rounds trying to track down Hutchinson.

Hutchinson’s win over Buatsi showed why he would be a problem fight for Canelo. He used his footwork to create space for counters and banked early rounds before Buatsi’s pressure and body work began to close the distance. Two judges scored the bout 115-113, proving Hutchinson can be made uncomfortable when forced to defend on the inside. For Canelo, the main question is whether he can apply steady pressure early enough to keep Hutchinson from building a large lead.

In past losses to Dmitry Bivol and Terence Crawford, Canelo struggled against fighters who controlled distance and refused to stand in front of him. Bivol used a jab to dictate the distance and fired combinations whenever Canelo stood behind his high guard. Crawford frequently changed angles, made Canelo miss, and countered before Canelo could move his feet. Hutchinson utilizes a similar formula. He scores with a sharp jab, follows up with quick combinations, and moves out of range before Canelo can return fire.

Against Mbilli in Riyadh, Canelo benefited from an opponent who marched forward and offered steady counterpunching opportunities. Hutchinson would force Canelo to be the aggressor, slip the initial shot, and exit before the second punch comes. Canelo carries the heavier power when he closes the distance, yet Hutchinson is capable of winning rounds on activity and movement while Canelo looks for a single opening. Allowing Hutchinson to control the early tempo would leave Canelo chasing the fight by the midpoint.

Canelo previously captured a light heavyweight title by stopping Sergey Kovalev in 2019 before dropping a decision to Bivol in his only other appearance at 175. Buatsi provided a workable blueprint for getting to Hutchinson through sustained forward pressure and targeted body shots. Canelo possesses the tools to execute that same game plan, provided he starts fast and stays committed even when Hutchinson makes him miss.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan Tells Eddie Hearn To Shut His Gob Over Fury vs. Joshua Undercard
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan is dead right to tell Eddie Hearn to shut his gob about the Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua undercard. Hearn has been running around bellyaching that the December 11 bill at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff is weak, even though he and Frank Warren spent years failing to make the main event happen themselves.

“If Eddie Hearn pops up telling you he could do an undercard that’s better, that’s fabulous, but you couldn’t make the main event. So sit down and shut up,” Jordan said on talkSPORT Boxing. “You and Frank [Warren], with respect, had years to make this fight.”

Now that somebody else finally got Fury and Joshua across the finish line, Hearn wants to act like he has all the answers for the undercard. The truth is, Hearn has no vision and no clue what fans actually want to see. Looking at the fights he floated to iFL TV, fans should be glad he is not running the show.

Hearn bragged to iFL TV that Joe Cordina had agreed to terms to face Manny Pacquiao, who turns 48 in December, and also wanted to throw Cordina in with WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason. Putting a Welsh two-time titleholder like Cordina on the card might please the local Cardiff crowd, as Jordan noted, but it does nothing for fans watching in the U.S. and Canada, and regular Brits barely care either. Zuffa got it right by leaving him off the show.

Giving a 34-year-old Cordina an undeserved title shot against Mason makes zero sense anyway. Cordina has not fought a good opponent since his eighth-round blowout loss to Anthony Cacace back in May 2024. That was ages ago, and beating Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz and Gabriel Flores Jr. since then does not earn him a shot at Mason.

Dragging a 47-year-old Pacquiao out to face Cordina is even worse. Pacquiao’s name might trick a few casual American fans into glancing at the poster, but nobody in North America is paying to watch Cordina. He was never a draw in America even when he held a belt at super featherweight.

The rest of Hearn’s matchmaking ideas are just as weak. Wanting Dave Allen to face Andy Ruiz Jr. or sticking Pacquiao in with Jack Catterall, Conah Walker, or Lewis Crocker sounds like a desperate attempt to unload Matchroom fighters onto a giant pay-per-view stage.

Jordan is dead right that the organizers need real fights before Fury and Joshua make their ring walks around 1 a.m., because fans shelling out big money deserve better than cheap filler. Hearn whining from the sidelines while pitching washed-up legends and domestic mismatches just proves Zuffa was smart to ignore him.

Ghana News.title: South Korea catches 111 students with new measures against exam cheating
Ghana News.content:
South Korea's education ministry says 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices during a high-stakes nationwide exam, after officials introduced urgent measures to tackle rising cases of AI-assisted cheating.

Five of the candidates were caught red-handed using smart devices during the exam, authorities said on Friday.

Half a million students sat for the college entry exam, also known as Suneung, which took place this week under the shadow of several recent high-profile cheating scandals.

Prior to the Suneung, authorities announced anti-cheating measures such as emergency alerts sent to every single mobile phone in the country to detect unauthorised devices in exam halls.

On Friday, Prime Minister Lee Jae Myung called for an overhaul of the exam system to tackle AI-assisted cheating.

In South Korea, public examinations "significantly affect the distribution of opportunities and resources", Lee said, adding that using AI to cheat in such tests "rocks the basic order of our society by undermining fairness and trust".

Concerns over academic dishonesty had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

Last month, two candidates were caught cheating with AI glasses during university entrance exams.

The education ministry said earlier this month that four students across middle and high schools were caught using AI glasses to cheat this year.

These fears came to a boil over the weekend, when the top scorer of South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam admitted to cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," said the candidate, 34-year-old Han Won-seok, in a video published on Sunday.

His confession, days ahead of the Suneung, prompted authorities to introduce last-minute measures to prevent cheating during the national exam.

The measures included nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea tapped on its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times that he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told news outlet Yonhap that he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams.

Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others.

The country itself comes to a standstill - construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment.

Many South Koreans see the Suneung as a culmination of years of formal education - and a turning point that determines their university placements, careers, and social statuses.

Ghana News.title: National Security arrests wanted pastor in counterfeit currency investigation
Ghana News.content:
A pastor who had been wanted by the National Security Secretariat since September over an alleged counterfeit currency operation has been arrested at Zenu, near Ashaiman, following months of investigations into a suspected network involved in producing and circulating fake banknotes.

The suspect was arrested on Wednesday, November 18, at a branch of his ministry in Klogon. Officers from the Secretariat’s Special Operations Directorate reportedly tracked him down after receiving intelligence about his whereabouts.

He is being investigated for conspiracy to counterfeit currency and other related offences. Following his arrest, he was transferred to the Bureau of National Investigations (BNI) for further questioning.

The pastor had reportedly been at large since June, when security operatives arrested several people suspected of involvement in the same operation during a raid at Lashibi.

His arrest is the latest development in investigations into a suspected counterfeiting network uncovered during a series of security operations in the Greater Accra Region earlier this year.

June raids uncovered suspected counterfeit currency centres

Between June 12 and July 24, security officers conducted six coordinated raids across parts of Greater Accra, uncovering four suspected counterfeit currency production facilities and arresting 16 people.

Details of the operations were subsequently disclosed by the National Security Secretariat in September.

One of the major operations took place on June 29, when security personnel searched an office at Lashibi before proceeding to the headquarters of a religious organisation at Klogon.

Read Also: Ghanaian pastor, Rev Emmanuel Boakye-Danquah on the run over alleged counterfeit currency syndicate

Investigators reportedly found that parts of the premises, including office spaces and residential accommodation, were allegedly being used to produce and store counterfeit currency.

Items seized included a printing machine, two vehicles and large quantities of unprinted currency coupons believed to have been intended for the production of fake banknotes.

The materials recovered during the operation at Klogon were estimated to be worth US$5.29 million, GH¢7.13 million and CFA623.53 million.

Millions in counterfeit notes and currency materials seized

Across the six operations, National Security said officers seized ready-to-circulate counterfeit notes amounting to US$543,000, GH¢196,600 and CFA60,000.

They also recovered unprinted currency coupons with estimated values of US$5.29 million, GH¢19.55 million and CFA623.55 million.

The 16 people arrested during the raids were transferred to the BNI, together with the seized items, for forensic examination and further investigations.

The Secretariat also said investigation dockets had been forwarded to the Attorney-General’s Department, with prosecutions underway at the Accra High Court.

The latest arrest is expected to contribute to ongoing investigations into the suspected network and the alleged roles of those involved.

Ghana News.title: Quality higher education comes at a cost: Who should pay?
Ghana News.content:
FM Dzanku · 20th November 2026 · Accra

Dealing with symptoms

The ongoing controversy over student hostel fees and the Minister of Education's directive to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) and the Rent Control Commission to explore their regulation should prompt a much broader national conversation about the financing of higher education in Ghana.

Earlier this year, GTEC directed the University of Ghana to reverse increases in academic fees, citing the need to comply with statutory procedures. While efforts to protect students from arbitrary and excessive charges are legitimate, we must confront a more fundamental question: how do we expect our public universities to deliver quality education without adequate financial resources?

Quality education is not cheap

Lecture rooms in our public universities continue to be overcrowded, student-to-lecturer ratios are unacceptably high, and teaching and learning facilities are overstretched. Universities struggle to recruit additional academic and non-academic staff because of government's financial constraints. Meanwhile, academic staff are poorly remunerated relative to the responsibilities placed on them, with limited funding for research.

Yet we expect these same universities to produce globally competitive graduates with the requisite skills to meet the demands of an increasingly sophisticated labour market.

We cannot continue to demand more from our public universities while constraining their ability to mobilise the resources needed to deliver.

Consider the case of Ashesi University, whose graduates are highly sought after by employers. Its impressive graduate employment outcomes and the quality of its graduates are well documented. But how often do we interrogate the circumstances under which these graduates are trained compared with those in our public universities?

Consider the differences in class sizes, student-to-lecturer ratios, contact hours, opportunities for individual academic engagement, teaching and learning facilities, and the overall learning environment.

These things cost money.

Undergraduate fees at Ashesi average GH¢60,331, nearly seven times the average at the University of Ghana when accommodation is included. Yet we expect our public universities to compete on quality without a commensurate investment in the educational process.

This is not necessarily a question of the competence of lecturers or the intellectual abilities of students in our public universities. In fact, some of the lecturers at Ashesi are from the public universities. It is more a question of the conditions under which teaching and learning take place.

Of course, higher fees do not automatically translate into better education. However, we cannot ignore the role of financial resources in creating an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning.

Affordability should not come at the expense of quality

The strongest argument against increasing university fees is, understandably, the risk of excluding students from poorer households. This is a legitimate concern, particularly in a country where socioeconomic circumstances already significantly shape educational opportunities.

But we must also recognise another form of inequality: inequality in the quality of education received.

If children from wealthier households can access better-resourced universities while those from poorer households are confined to chronically underfunded institutions, have we really addressed inequality of educational opportunity?

Access to higher education is important, but so is access to quality higher education.

Rather than suppressing fees across the board, irrespective of the financial circumstances of students and the cost of delivering quality education, we should explore a more sustainable and equitable financing model.

Such a model could combine adequate and predictable public funding, realistic cost recovery fees, means-tested scholarships and grants, and accessible student loans with repayment arrangements linked to graduates' earnings.

This must be accompanied by strong accountability mechanisms to ensure that additional resources translate into measurable improvements in educational quality.

THE CORE PROBLEMWe expect our public universities to deliver quality higher education, yet we have failed to establish a sustainable and equitable financing model that makes this possible without excluding those who cannot afford to pay.

Someone has to pay

Higher education generates both private and societal benefits. There is, therefore, a strong economic justification for sharing its cost between the state and its beneficiaries, with adequate safeguards for those who cannot afford to pay.

If government wants public universities to maintain low fees, it must be prepared to finance the difference between what students pay and what it costs to deliver quality education.

Simply directing universities not to increase fees does not make the cost of providing education disappear. It merely leaves the question of who bears that cost unanswered.

Ghana needs a serious national conversation about higher education financing that goes beyond the periodic controversies over academic and hostel fees.

Our policy objective should not simply be to make higher education affordable. It should be to make quality higher education affordable.

There is an important difference.

THE BOTTOM LINEQuality higher education costs money, and someone has to pay. The solution is not to suppress fees at the expense of quality, but to ensure that no qualified student is denied quality education because of an inability to pay.

FM Dzanku, 20th November 2026, Accra

Ghana News.title: Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation
Ghana News.content:
A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned.

Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.

France has blamed Iran for one of the waves of attacks that impacted its supermarkets, a claim Tehran denies.

It was thought the UK had largely escaped such hacks as the British refrigeration industry relies on different devices but there was in fact a potential vulnerability the sector has been rushing to fix.

In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK.

Since then, researchers, IT teams and the National Cyber Security Centre have been working around the clock to warn dozens of companies.

The BBC has not reported on the large-scale, secretive operation until now to reduce the chances of hackers causing harm if they found the vulnerability.

Thousands of fridges taken off-line

The security threat was discovered by staff at refrigeration consultants Omega Solutions - it was then verified and expanded upon by experts at Pen Test Partners who helped raise the alarm.

The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) and Food Standards Agency (FSA) were then involved in the campaign to plug the security holes.

They held industry conference calls and tasked teams to contact firms at risk.

Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration devices were taken off the open internet either remotely or, in some cases, physically - with staff ordered to remove internet cables and monitor temperatures manually.

BBC news has learnt most major supermarkets have been forced to divert IT teams to address the risks, with a worker at one large chain saying they took hundreds of devices offline every day over the course of a week.

"It did feel like a race against time as we were expecting another wave of these fridge hacks to come," said the person, who did not want to be publicly named.

"From a business perspective it could have been potentially devastating with business interruption and supply chain problems. Our warehouses have millions of pounds worth of food that could have been spoiled if any hackers found out about this method of attack," they added.

There have been three waves of hacks on refrigeration temperature controllers so far this year:

In August, fridges at a small number of US military bases were impacted

On 11 and 12 October hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites in France were hit when Danfoss temperature control systems were targeted

On 1 and 2 November dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries were hit, with Belgium and Luxembourg the worst affected. A small number of blood bank sites in France were also impacted

The waves of attacks prompted an expert at Omega Solutions to examine the security of the most popular refrigeration controllers in the UK, made by British firm Resource Data Management (RDM).

RDM disputes the critical nature of the vulnerabilities exposed but has been praised for its professional response to address the concerns, the BBC understands.

As well as supermarkets, multiple other areas of UK food and beverage industry were also warned to take action about the risks.

These include convenience stores, petrol stations, restaurants and fast food chains, sports arenas, hotels, food processing plants and cold storage sites.

"These popular controllers had a similar weak password problem to the Danfoss and other controllers that were attacked so successfully in previous hacks so we had to get the message out as soon as possible and keep it secret," said Ken Munro of Pen Test Partners.

"There is so much extra attention on these ubiquitous bits of kit now that it was likely a matter of days until criminals or nation state hackers figured it out," he added.

RDM, though, says comparisons with the units attacked in mainland Europe are not fair because hacking their fridges and freezers would have involved getting hold of a piece of hardware.

The ethical hackers say this would have been achievable as the hardware in question can be purchased cheaply online on sites like eBay.

"This was a vulnerability identified in a test environment," said Ged Evans, CEO of RDM.

He said the test "went beyond" what such exercises usually involved, as it "included dismantling our hardware".

"In any event we have acted at pace to address this issue and have already deployed first patch releases and have been in proactive contact with our customers to flag any issues and recommend mitigatory steps," he added.

RDM confirmed that there was no sign of any malicious activity on the controllers and that it continued to work with the NCSC and other authorities to monitor the situation.

Ghana News.title: Trump posthumously pardons US baseball legend, Pete Rose
Ghana News.content:
US President Donald Trump has posthumously pardoned baseball legend Pete Rose.

"I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday.

Rose, who died in 2024 at the age of 83, pleaded guilty in 1990 to two counts of filing false tax returns. He was also given a lifetime ban from Major League Baseball (MLB) after an investigation revealed he bet on games.

The baseball star was posthumously reinstated to MLB, in which he played for 24 seasons, last year and made eligible for the Baseball Hall of Fame.

Trump also said on Thursday that Rose's "record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken".

In fact, Rose accumulated a record 4,256 hits - which MLB defines as a batter striking the baseball into fair territory and reaching base without doing so via an error or a fielder's choice - during his career, which is more than any other player. He played a total of 3,562 games.

According to Trump, Rose "was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame. Politics, I guess".

The US Constitution gives a sitting president the broad power to grant a pardon, which represents legal forgiveness and ends any further punishment.

Because Rose's pardon was issued after his death, it is largely symbolic and does not change Rose's Hall of Fame status. The Department of Justice (DoJ) typically does not process posthumous pardon applications, though presidents have still issued them.

The BBC has contacted the Hall of Fame and the DoJ for comment.

The US president had previously floated the idea of pardoning Rose in March last year before the MLB reinstated him.

"Major League Baseball didn't have the courage or decency to put the late, great Pete Rose, also known as 'Charlie Hustle,' into the Baseball Hall of Fame," he wrote on Truth Social at the time.

"Now he is dead, will never experience the thrill of being selected, even though he was a FAR BETTER PLAYER than most of those who made it, and can only be named posthumously. WHAT A SHAME," Trump added.

MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred issued a decision in May 2025 that created a pathway for Rose to be eligible to be inducted into the baseball Hall of Fame - a ruling that also applied to 16 other people - as early as 2028.

In August 1989, Rose agreed to the permanent ban from the sport after MLB investigators found that he bet on his team, the Cincinnati Reds, multiple times while he was playing on and managing the team from 1985 to 1987.

In July 1990, after Rose admitted to failing to report $354,968 (£271,107) in income over a four-year period, he was sentenced to five months in prison. He was also fined $50,000 and ordered to perform community service at the time.
