World.title: Orea Botanica Makes official debut in Lagos, reimaging ritual of body care
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Bennett Oghifo

Oréa Botanica, a premium wellness and body-care brand inspired by African botanical intelligence and informed by modern skincare science, has officially unveiled its vision with an exclusive brand launch at Polo Avenue, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Friday, November 13, 2026.

The evening welcomed a mix of personalities across fashion, media, entertainment and business, including Dr Morayo Afolabi-Brown, Andrea Iyamah, Tania Omotayo and Sandrah Tubobereni (TUBO), among others.

The event’s conversations centred around beauty, wellness, self-care and intentional living, celebrating the vision of the two women behind the brand.

Founded by Yetunde Demuren, with Ora Mantu as Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer, Oréa Botanica was created to bring African botanical knowledge into contemporary wellness, and recognising the value of traditional beauty rituals while embracing the possibilities of modern skincare science.

At its core, the brand seeks to move everyday body care beyond routine, encouraging a more intentional approach to self-care, self-preservation and elevation.

Founder, Yetunde Demuren, stated that “the foundation of every good skincare brand should always be the art of natural radiance; nourishment, protection and illumination. At Orea, our philosophy is Afro-Minimalism, essence not excess.”

This philosophy informs the brand’s approach to product development, bringing together botanical inspiration, carefully considered ingredients and modern formulation principles.

Through this blend, Oréa Botanica aims to create body-care experiences that are both purposeful and pleasurable, making everyday self-care an opportunity to nourish the skin and reconnect with oneself.

Co-Founder/COO, Ora Mantu introduced guests to the story behind the brand’s name, explaining that Oréa was coined from a combination of both founders’ names.

According to her, “Oréa Botanica means golden and glow in Latin, reflecting the essence of the brand and its vision for elevated wellness.”

The brand’s inaugural body-care collection, comprises three products: Polish, Exfoliating Body Scrub; Illuminate, Restorative Body Oil; and Quench, Nourishing Body Butter. Each product plays a role in the brand’s approach to a considered body-care ritual.

Adding an educational dimension to the experience, cosmetic scientist, Hilary Rodriguez-Taiwo, popularly known as Hilary Says, explained: that “Polish features papaya enzymes, Himalayan Desert Salt and Lactic Acid which help loosen and remove dead skin cells, while Quench contains a trio of Shea, Cocoa, Mango Seed Butter, Niacinamide and Alpha-Arbutin, ingredients selected to support skin health, and Illuminate features a blend of ethnobotanical oils, Retinol and Vitamin C which helps to even skin tone and smooth skin texture.”

Her presentation gave guests a closer understanding of the role of carefully selected ingredients in effective body care and the relationship between botanical inspiration and informed formulation.

More than a product unveiling, the launch introduced Oréa Botanica’s wider vision: one that recognises the richness of African botanical heritage while embracing a contemporary understanding of beauty and wellness.

According to the brand, “To discover Oréa Botanica and explore its collection, visit @oreabotanica_ on Instagram or oreabotanica.com .”

By bringing these perspectives together, Orea hopes to make intentional self-care more meaningful, with products that encourage consumers to prioritise nourishment, protection and balance in their everyday lives.

World.title: Tinubu Urges Youths to Draw Lessons from Lott-Jonathan’s Memoir
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Ayodeji Ake

President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths, particularly young women, to draw lessons from the life experiences of Dr. Ayima Lott-Jonathan as documented in her memoir, “Gold Dust: Treasures of Quiet Years”.

Tinubu, who was represented by the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Voice of Nigeria, Mallam Jibrin Baba Ndace, at the public presentation of the book in Abuja yesterday, said the memoir offered valuable lessons on courage, patience, perseverance and purposeful living.

The president described the book as more than a record of personal experiences, saying it provided an opportunity to preserve memories, share lessons and pass valuable insights from one generation to another.

He said the memoir opened a window into the author’s journey, reflecting on faith, family, motherhood, perseverance, challenges and the pursuit of purpose.

According to him, the title, Gold Dust, captures the value of lessons that emerge from life’s experiences, including difficult moments.

“Her story reminds us that courage, patience and service give meaning to life. We have heard how she did not pretend to have had a perfect life.

She shared moments that were difficult for her and offered lessons that others can learn from,” he said.

Tinubu urged young Nigerians to reflect on the experiences documented in the book, adding: “I hope this book will inspire young people, particularly women, to remain committed to their aspirations and understand that their experiences can become a source of inspiration and empowerment for others.”

He also emphasised the importance of preserving Nigeria’s cultural heritage and strengthening the contribution of the creative industry to national development.

Similarly, former Vice President, Mohammed Namadi Sambo, who chaired the occasion, described the memoir as a story of resilience, determination, courage, sacrifice and strength of character.

Sambo, whose speech was read by Ahmed Modibbo, said: “Gold Dust is more than a personal account of life’s experiences. It is a story of resilience, determination, courage, sacrifice, achievements and the strength of character required to navigate life’s challenges.”

He noted that Nigerian society needed more stories celebrating positive role models, particularly women whose contributions to family, professional life, community development and national progress deserved greater recognition.

“The experiences documented in this memoir remind us that women have always played indispensable roles in shaping our society and nation,” he said.

Sambo further described the title as symbolic, arguing that the true worth of a person’s life was determined not merely by material accomplishments or public recognition but by character, lives touched, challenges overcome and the legacy left behind.

He urged young Nigerians, especially women, to understand that success required discipline, courage, patience, faith and an unwavering commitment to their aspirations.

In her remarks, Lott-Jonathan, a spouse of former President Goodluck Jonathan, said she deliberately chose Aduvie International School, Abuja, which she founded in 2008, as the venue for the presentation because the institution represented where much of her life’s work had been accomplished.

“Many of you are meeting me today as a birthday celebrant and an author. But this hall, this campus and the children whose voices you will hear later this morning represent where most of my life’s work has been done. It feels right that the story of that life should be launched here, at home,” she said.

Explaining the title, she said her 50 years had been shaped by different experiences, sacrifices, opportunities and painful moments.

“That is how I have come to see my 50 years. They have not been one dramatic event. They have been grains: a lesson from my father, a sacrifice from my mother, a word of encouragement from a teacher, a door opened by a stranger, an introduction by an uncle, and a loss that taught me what really matters,” she said.

The 12-chapter memoir chronicles her childhood in Famgbe, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, her four-year wait for university admission, legal education and professional career, as well as her eventual transition into educational leadership.

She recounted how a conversation with her daughter’s teacher inspired the establishment of Aduvie International School, which started in 2008 in a five-bedroom bungalow in Wuse, Abuja, with four staff members and two pupils. The school has since grown to serve more than 1,000 children.

The author also reflected on personal challenges, including the loss of two younger brothers, Ekiye and Boinime, and her experiences of waiting and delayed fulfilment.

“I have not hidden the hard chapters. I have learned that they are often where the gold is,” she said.

Lott-Jonathan, who dedicated the memoir to her husband, described service as the guiding philosophy behind her life’s work, citing the Latin expression, “Non nobis, sed aliis” (Not for ourselves, but for others).

She said: “I believe that the true measure of what we build is not merely what we achieve for ourselves, but what we leave behind for others to inherit, enjoy and build upon.”

World.title: Violence: Edo South ADC Candidate Raises the Alarm  over Security Breaches, Wants Govt’s Intervention
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) senatorial candidate for Edo South, Matthew Iduoriyekemwen, has raised concerns over reported security breaches in his ancestral community of Amagba, Oredo Local Government Area of Edo State, calling on the state government and security agencies to intervene to prevent further escalation.

Iduoriyekemwen appealed ahead of the January 16, 2027 elections, following a reported security incident in the community on November 12, 2026.

Speaking with journalists in Benin City, the former Majority Leader of the Edo State House of Assembly urged his supporters to remain calm and ensure that the development does not distract them from their political activities ahead of the elections.

He said he received reports from relatives in the early hours of November 12 about the presence of some individuals allegedly accompanied by armed operatives of the local security corps in the community.

According to him, gunshots were reportedly fired during the incident, forcing some residents to flee their homes for fear for their safety.

The incident came weeks after the reported arrest of his 90-year-old father, Pa Joseph Iduoriyekemwen, the traditional head (Odionwere) of Amagba.

The nonagenarian was reportedly handed over to the Edo State Police Command for questioning before being arraigned in court over allegations his son has disputed.

The ADC candidate also expressed concern over alleged moves to remove his father from his traditional position, insisting that due process must be followed and the rights of all parties respected.

Against this backdrop, he appealed to the Edo State Government and relevant security agencies to urgently intervene to restore peace and prevent further deterioration of the situation.

“I am concerned about the developments in my ancestral community, particularly the reported incident of November 12 and the earlier arrest and arraignment of my father. I appeal to all concerned to exercise restraint and allow the appropriate authorities to address the issues,” he said.

The former Edo State representative on the Board of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) maintained that disputes involving land, boundaries and traditional leadership should be resolved through established legal and traditional institutions rather than actions capable of creating tension and threatening communal peace.

He urged the state government to ensure that the Amagba situation is handled fairly and transparently, irrespective of political affiliations.

Iduoriyekemwen further appealed to ADC members and voters across the seven local government areas of Edo South senatorial district-Oredo, Egor, Ikpoba-Okha, Ovia North-East, Ovia South-West, Orhionmwon and Uhunmwonde-to remain peaceful and focused on the forthcoming elections.

“My message to our supporters across all seven local government areas of Edo South is clear: remain peaceful, stay focused and refuse to be provoked into violence,” he said.

He urged party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through peaceful campaigns, door-to-door engagements and direct interactions with voters across the senatorial district.

Expressing confidence in the electoral process, the ADC candidate said the January 16, 2027, election should reflect the genuine wishes of the electorate.

He stressed that voters must be allowed to freely exercise their democratic rights without intimidation, harassment,t or interference.

World.title: Turn Hunger Pledges into Laws, Budgets, Obasa Tasks  Global Lawmakers
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yusuf Ebiti

The Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Mudashiru Ajayi Obasa, has urged parliamentarians worldwide to convert commitments against hunger and malnutrition into concrete laws, budgets, and oversight mechanisms.

Obasa made this call at the Third Global Parliamentary Summit on Hunger and Malnutrition held in Kenya in Nairobi. It is the first time the summit has been held in Africa.

According to a statement, represented by a high-powered delegation of legislators, senior assembly staff, and senior legislative aides, Obasa shared Nigeria’s and Lagos State’s experiences and outlined both the legislative steps already taken and those still required.

He said: “We are not treating the issues of hunger and malnutrition in Lagos or Nigeria with levity. Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, the Federal Government has approved the National Nutrition Bill 2026 and the revised National Policy on Food and Nutrition.

“The approvals will help to establish a comprehensive framework for strengthening governance, sustainable funding mechanisms for nutrition programmes, improving institutional coordination, and ensuring effective implementation of food and nutrition interventions nationwide.”

On Lagos State’s part, Obasa noted that the state, with limited arable land and over 22 million residents, cannot significantly expand farmland. Instead, it is prioritising productivity, efficiency, and strategic partnerships through a five-point strategy centred on technology, interstate collaboration, investment in farmers, reduction of post-harvest losses, and improved access to affordable, nutritious food.

He highlighted major interventions by the state government, including the Imota Rice Mill, a large-scale agricultural and industrial facility located in Ikorodu, inaugurated in January 2023.

With a capacity to produce 2.8 million 50kg bags of rice yearly while generating 1,500 direct jobs and 254,000 indirect jobs for residents and citizens alike, it stands as the largest rice mill in Sub-Saharan Africa and one of the largest globally.

Obasa also cited the N500 billion Offtake Guarantee Fund ‘Produce for Lagos’ Initiative, a state government-led collaboration with the private sector to tackle supply chain inefficiencies and enhance access to agricultural produce.

This also aims to provide working capital for bulk traders and logistics operators, and credit support for food producers across the state to ensure a stable food supply for Lagos and beyond while boosting private sector investment in agriculture and food systems.

As part of this initiative, the Lagos Fresh Food Hub, Obasa said, had already constructed and inaugurated functional mid-level food hub facilities in Mushin, Abijo (Ibeju-Lekki), and Agege while construction of its 500-hectare central food logistics hub has reached 70 per cent completion.

The facility, located in Epe, Lagos State, is expected to feature cold-chain storage, dry-chain infrastructure and other facilities intended to improve food handling and distribution. It will also address challenges affecting the preservation, transportation, and distribution of agricultural produce.

On the legislative front, Obasa emphasised concrete actions already taken.

He said: “In September 2021, the Lagos State House of Assembly passed the Anti-Open Grazing of Livestock Law, which makes it unlawful for cattle rearers to occupy unapproved public areas and private land with their livestock for grazing. It also prohibits the act of moving cattle around public places by herders.“Through our Appropriation Laws, we have prioritised the agriculture and food systems sector, allocating more than N80 billion across recent budget cycles. We are currently advancing the Food Hub Bill, which will formalise market operations, reduce the constraints of informal trading, improve food safety standards, and strengthen coordination across the value chain.”

He added that legislation, adequate funding, and rigorous oversight remain essential:

“As legislators, we back every effort to combat hunger and malnutrition with concrete laws and oversight. The Lagos State House of Assembly will continue to deepen this work. We will maintain and increase budgetary allocations for resilient agrifood systems. We will strengthen oversight mechanisms and refine laws to promote climate-smart agriculture.”

He concluded by reaffirming Lagos State’s readiness to share experiences and collaborate with other legislatures: “Lagos stands ready to share its experiences, to learn from the innovations of other legislatures across the world, and to work in solidarity with every parliament represented here. Together, let us legislate for a hunger-free future.”

The two-day summit, organised by the Parliament of Kenya, the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO), and the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), brought together more than 200 parliamentarians from over 60 countries. The theme was “Legislating for Resilient Agrifood Systems and Zero Hunger in a Changing Climate.”

In his keynote address, President William Ruto of Kenya said ending hunger requires legislation, budgets, and oversight, which are parliaments’ core responsibilities. He warned that Africa could account for nearly 60 per cent of the world’s hungry by 2030 if action is not accelerated, despite holding more than 60 per cent of the world’s remaining uncultivated arable land.

He further called for domestic resource mobilisation, reduced reliance on food imports, stronger irrigation, expanded school feeding programmes, and laws protecting food-security programmes from political cycles. President Ruto underscored his message with the memorable line: “A right without a budget line is a slogan.”

World.title: Oniha Commends Progress On Kaduna-Kano Rail Project, Says Funding Will Follow Due Process
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

•December inauguration on course, says Adebiyi

Kasim Sumaina in Kano

The Director General of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Mrs.Patience Oniha Thursday commended the Ministry of Transportation and contractors handling the Kaduna-Kano rail project for the remarkable progress recorded within a short period.

The DG, who was on an inspection visit with the Permanent Secretary, Ministry Engr. Funso Adebiyi and two of her colleagues, said the DMO, as the government agency that provides funding and financing for capital projects, was at the site to appreciate the work being done with government funds.

“We are a government agency that provides funding, financing for capital projects like that. So our coming here is part of appreciating the work that is being done by the government using those funds,” she said.

She said it was important to see the work done since the last visit, noting the significant improvement in travel experience. “The last time we came, we rove by road from Kaduna to this place. But today we rove by train from Abuja to Kaduna, and then on a short ride we got into Jaji, and here we are in a short while without any hitches in Kano,” she said.

According to her, the government is providing alternative means of transport, which goes beyond just moving people and cargo. “When you have transport, things happen on the sites. They are traded, selling things, whether it is food, whatever. So it’s not just building the rails and moving people and moving cargo, there’s so much for the small businessman and woman to do along that corridor.”

On the need for more funding for the project, the DG said funding would be processed once projects are evaluated and approved. “As the projects come, we have to evaluate, obviously we have to evaluate, we have to know what it is being used for, and then we process appraisals. We are here because funding was provided, so that is not the issue. It is to process it and get it ready. It has to start with the Ministry of Transportation anyway, but we work very closely, so that is not an issue. Once the government understands it, we go through the approval process and the funding comes,” she explained.

She also expressed delight at the quality of work at the station building, describing it as wonderful and excellent. “It will be unfair for me to leave this place without commenting on this wonderful, excellent building that we’ve seen. The last time we came, I think it was a bit dark and we were working very carefully, but it’s amazing to see the amount of work that has been done between that last time and now, which is a very short period,” she said.

“We have seen rail stations, stations, we have seen airports. I mean, this is excellent job that has been done, and done not only for the people of Kano to use, because this will also be a transit point, so the benefits are immense,” she added.

She commended the Ministry of Transportation as well as the contractors for their commitment.

“I’d really like to commend the Ministry of Transportation as well as the contractors. They listen, they are committed, and they are doing a good job,” she said.

Speaking in similar vein, the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi, has expressed satisfaction with the level of progress recorded on the Kaduna–Kano Railway Project, declaring that the project, including its train stations, has reached an advanced stage and is ready for commissioning as scheduled.

Describing the train journey as seamless, delightful and highly commendable, Adebiyi said the Kano Terminal Station was substantially ready, with only the installation of its name signage outstanding, which he expected to be completed within the next two weeks.

The Permanent Secretary recalled that during his previous inspection, he had identified certain areas requiring improvement, not necessarily because the contractors had performed poorly, but to ensure that the project met the highest possible standards. He expressed satisfaction that the issues raised had been adequately addressed.

One of the major improvements, he explained, was the replacement of toughened glass with laminated glass in passenger-accessible areas. According to him, laminated glass offers enhanced safety because, unlike toughened glass, it does not shatter into potentially dangerous fragments under certain conditions. In the event of damage, only the affected section would require replacement.

He also disclosed that he had insisted on the use of station lighting bulbs with a minimum serviceability lifespan of three years, adding that the contractors had complied with the directive by replacing the bulbs to meet the required specifications.

Other improvements included the provision of man-lifts to facilitate maintenance activities and arrangements for the training of Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC) engineers in station operations.

Adebiyi said the NRC had been directed to nominate engineers for the training, which he would personally attend, stressing that only those who successfully pass the required examinations would be retained to operate the facilities.

On the commencement of commercial operations, the Permanent Secretary disclosed that the Ministry was making a case for a three-month test run of the railway from Jaji to Kano, potentially as a free passenger service, subject to the approval of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. He explained that the exercise would provide an opportunity to assess the structural integrity and operational performance of the railway before full commercial services commence.

He expressed confidence in the quality of the track infrastructure, noting that the smoothness of the journey during the inspection was evident, as passengers could comfortably drink tea, take soft drinks and eat without experiencing noticeable vibrations or shaking.

On accessibility, Adebiyi said provisions had been made to accommodate persons with disabilities, following observations from his previous inspection. He disclosed that about four lifts had been ordered to improve accessibility, while an additional staircase had been introduced at the rear of the terminal. Railings for the staircase had also been imported to facilitate safe and convenient movement within the facility.

He described the Kano Terminal Station’s waiting hall as exceptional, expressing the view that it could rank among the best railway terminal facilities in Africa. He commended the contractors for the overall quality of work delivered.

Speaking on the remaining connection between Kaduna and Kano, Adebiyi explained that the security considerations around Jaji necessitated the introduction of a horizontal curve along the alignment, resulting in the construction of a bridge.

He said the bridge, which is being constructed in-situ, is at an advanced stage of completion. According to him, it represents the major outstanding infrastructure between the Jaji section and the connection to Kaduna. He added that track-related works had progressed to the bridge embankment and that rail laying would commence upon completion of the structure.

The Permanent Secretary further disclosed that the Kaduna Train Station, where passengers would alight, was undergoing expansion to accommodate the anticipated increase in passenger traffic.

He also revealed that construction was ongoing on another railway corridor originating from Kano and extending through Kazaure, Daura and Katsina. He said the inspection team was scheduled to visit the corridor the following morning, noting that the project had encountered some land acquisition challenges between the Kano station and Dawano. However, the alignment from Dawano through Kazaure and Daura to Katsina was progressing.

Providing a broader perspective on the Federal Government’s railway development programme, the Permanent Secretary explained that the Kaduna–Kano corridor forms part of an integrated national railway network designed to connect major commercial and industrial centres across the country.

He noted that the railway network originates from Apapa in Lagos, allowing 40-foot containers to be transported by rail to Ibadan, where a dry port provides facilities for cargo clearance.

Speaking further, the Permanent Secretary said the broader connectivity plan would link Abuja to Kaduna, Kaduna to Zaria, Zaria to Kano, and further extend through Kazaure, Daura and Katsina.

According to him, the railway development programme is being implemented as an integrated national infrastructure initiative rather than a series of isolated projects.

He therefore, expressed optimism that, upon completion of the planned railway connections, passengers would be able to travel by rail from Warri through Kano, Katsina, Daura and Kazaure, with further connectivity extending from Katsina to Jibia and Maradi in the Republic of Niger.

World.title: High tree pollen levels could trigger allergies in three cities
World.content:
A tree releasing pollen into the air, highlighting a natural source of seasonal allergies. Image: Pexels

People living with allergies in Johannesburg, Kimberley and Potchefstroom could face more symptoms as tree pollen levels remain high.

The latest pollen report shows high tree pollen concentrations in all three cities, with olive pollen emerging as a major contributor in Johannesburg and Potchefstroom.

Kimberley recorded high levels of several tree pollens, with plane trees dominating.



For allergy sufferers, this means outdoor exposure could trigger sneezing, a runny or blocked nose, itchy eyes and other allergic reactions.

Johannesburg: Olive pollen dominates

Johannesburg recorded high tree pollen concentrations, with olive pollen among the dominant types.

Other trees releasing pollen include birch, false olive, bushwillow, cypress, ebony, mulberry, gum, oak and karee.



Weed pollen levels remained low, while mould concentrations were moderate.

People who react to pollen should take precautions when spending time outdoors, particularly if they already experience seasonal allergy symptoms.

Kimberley: High tree pollen levels

Kimberley also recorded high tree pollen concentrations, with plane trees dominating the sample.



Other pollen sources included birch, bushwillow, ash, mulberry, olive, poplar, karee and elm.

Grass pollen levels were moderate, while weed pollen and mould concentrations remained low.

Potchefstroom: Olive pollen remains high

Potchefstroom recorded high tree pollen levels, with olive pollen dominating.



Grass pollen levels remained low, while the report also detected low concentrations of weed pollen and mould.

Cape Town and Bloemfontein recorded moderate grass pollen levels.

Cape Town had low tree pollen concentrations, with several types of trees, weeds and moulds detected.



Bloemfontein recorded high tree pollen concentrations, with olive among the dominant trees.

Other identified sources included acacia, birch, false olive, hackberry, bushwillow, gum, oak, pine, plane, poplar and karee.

Pretoria, Durban and Gqeberha record low pollen levels

Pretoria recorded low concentrations across the pollen categories, although the report noted strong peaks of Cladosporium, an allergenic mould.



Durban and Gqeberha also recorded low, grass and weed pollen concentrations.

Mould levels remained low at both sites, although Durban recorded peaks in basidiospores, which include mushroom spores.

George’s pollen monitoring station has resumed operations following a long break caused by relocation.



The latest sample showed low, grass and weed pollen levels, although rain may have reduced the recorded concentrations.

World.title: This affordable retirement coastal town just got a property below R100 000
World.content:
Mtwalume on KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast is one of a handful of coastal towns where pensioners can live comfortably on R6 000 a month.

The town first became a popular holiday spot in 1901, when the South Coast rail launched.

Since then, a handful of luxury seaside homes and villas have slowly overtaken the unspoilt coastline. But many modest, simple luxuries still exist throughout the town.



Building a dream coastal home on a R95 000 plot

A 550-square-metre plot in the coastal town of Mtwalume recently went to market with a R95 000 asking price.

The plot in a security estate on Cowey Road was listed on 16 October by RE/MAX Scottsburgh and is officially the only coastal plot in South Africa currently on the market for less than R100 000.

But Mtwalume’s uniqueness isn’t limited to one affordable plot.

Homes in the region start at a surprisingly low R200 000.

These fibreglass and timber homes in resort-style estates are available to cash buyers.

More than a dozen homes in the seaside town are on the market for below R500 000.



For a modern, move-in-ready townhouse, buyers can get a 2-bedroom duplex for R600 000.

Levies are rarely more than R1 800 a month.

This affordability has attracted a large retired community, with roughly 80% of residents being over 50.

Buying a home in Mtwalume

The town is a haven for water-loving South Africans.

From the shore and along the hillside, you can see bottlenose, common, and humpback dolphins.

Residents and visitors alike can enjoy the tidal pools, lagoon, and the Mtwalume River.

Much of the area’s coastline is unspoilt and peaceful.

Getting a property for below R500 000 on such a pristine coast can feel like a dream.

However, being surrounded by water also means the area is frequently affected by flooding.

In 2022, Gift of the Givers rebuilt houses in Mtwalume destroyed in the floods.

Days of heavy rain caused fatal flooding and, in the aftermath, homeowners had to deal with property damage and mould, worsened by the area’s humidity.

These severe conditions can occur year-round.

The flooding in 2022 occurred in April.

This year, officials are on high alert in November about potential flooding in the town.

For this reason, many residents won’t splurge on luxury homes with higher rebuild costs and insurance premiums.

Instead, they turn to modest homes that are cheap to fix.

But sometimes these properties can also be more susceptible to damage.

In some cases, these affordable plots and homes have the highest risk of damage.

World.title: Metrorail ticket price increases begin on 1 December. Here are your new fares
World.content:
Metrorail commuters will pay more for monthly tickets from 1 December 2026. Image: Prasa Group/Facebook

Metrorail commuters face higher monthly ticket prices from 1 December 2026, following a fare adjustment announced by the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA).

The increase is part of a phased adjustment affecting monthly tickets only. Single and weekly fares will remain unchanged for now.

PRASA says the changes follow further stakeholder consultations, which concluded in October 2026. The agency is implementing the increases in stages to limit the financial impact on commuters.



New Metrorail monthly ticket prices from December

The first phase of the adjustment applies to monthly tickets covering 52 trips, from Monday to Saturday.

Depending on the travel distance, commuters will pay between R35 and R46 more per month.

Here is a breakdown of the new fares:

Travel distance Current monthly fare Increase New fare from 1 December 1–15km R180 R35 R215 16–40km R220 R46 R266 41–60km R250 R41 R291 More than 61km R280 R42 R322

Despite the increases, PRASA says monthly tickets remain considerably cheaper than buying individual daily tickets.

For example, a commuter travelling between 1km and 15km would spend R520 on daily tickets over the same monthly period. The new monthly ticket costs R215, saving R305.

PRASA says the additional revenue will help fund energy costs, train and infrastructure maintenance, and improved safety and security.



More ticket price increases could follow in 2027

The December adjustment is only the first phase of a wider fare restructuring.

A second phase will combine the outstanding approved increase with a Consumer Price Index (CPI)-linked adjustment. It will apply to all ticket types, including single and weekly tickets.

Implementation is targeted for no earlier than 1 April 2027. However, this remains subject to further consultation and final approval.

PRASA Group CEO Hishaam Emeran acknowledged the impact of fare increases on commuters.

“We understand that any change in the cost of travel matters to the households we serve,” he said.

Emeran added that the revenue would support “safer and more reliable trains.”

PRASA also confirmed that daily off-peak discounts will remain in place. Commuters travelling between 09:30 and 14:30 can still benefit from discounts of up to 50% on daily fares.

The agency says it intends to introduce annual Consumer Price Index (CPI)-linked adjustments in future, indicatively between 4% and 4.5%.

World.title: Rare black springbok born months after death of beloved Siya
World.content:
A rare black springbok has been born at Kingswood Golf Estate in George, bringing excitement to the estate and reviving memories of Siya, its much-loved black springbok that died earlier this year. Image: Corneli Dittrich

A rare black springbok has been born at Kingswood Golf Estate in George, bringing excitement to the estate and reviving memories of Siya, its much-loved black springbok that died earlier this year.

The newest addition to Kingswood’s wildlife population was born earlier this month.

The arrival is particularly significant for the estate, which welcomed its first black springbok on 4 October 2024.



The youngster was named Siya following suggestions from the public and soon became something of a local celebrity, attracting attention from residents, golfers and wildlife enthusiasts across the country.

Remembering Siya

For almost two years, Siya was a familiar sight on the estate’s fairways and open spaces. Residents, golfers and visitors often looked forward to spotting the distinctive antelope, whose unusual colouring made him one of Kingswood’s most recognisable wildlife residents.

However, Kingswood announced his death in July this year, when he was just under two years old.



A post-mortem examination confirmed that Siya had died of natural causes, bringing some closure to those who had grown fond of him.

In a tribute, the estate said: “While his time with us was far too short, the memories he created will endure, and he will be fondly remembered as a special part of the Kingswood family.”

His loss was deeply felt by the many people who had come to know and appreciate him.



The birth of another black springbok has therefore been met with particular excitement, bringing a welcome new chapter to Kingswood’s wildlife story.

What makes a black springbok so rare?

Unlike the more familiar tan-and-white springbok, black springbok have a distinctive dark coat caused by melanism – a naturally occurring genetic variation that results in increased dark pigmentation.

They are not a separate species, but a colour variation of the springbok.



The latest arrival is also part of a growing springbok population at Kingswood. Four other youngsters born earlier are reportedly thriving, while more births have been observed on the estate.

Wildlife on the fairways

The births highlight the rich wildlife that forms part of everyday life at Kingswood, where golfers and residents regularly encounter animals roaming the estate.

For those who remember Siya, the newest black springbok is an especially welcome addition. While it cannot replace the much-loved animal, its arrival gives residents another opportunity to follow the development of one of nature’s more unusual colour variations.

World.title: Springboks forced into late team change
World.content:
It’s already been a chaotic week for the Springboks as they prepare to face Ireland on Saturday, and now Ruan Nortje has been forced to withdraw from the team on Friday due to a niggle picked up at training this week.

Instead, Franco Mostert will start Saturday’s Nations Championship encounter against Ireland in Dublin at lock next to Eben Etzebeth.

Nortje has been monitored by the medical team throughout the week, but Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus opted to take a cautious approach on Friday morning.



Although the Springboks will be comfortable with the inclusion of the experienced Mostert, it can’t be overlooked how important Nortje has become to the national cause, quietly having established himself as the first-choice No 5 lock in recent seasons.

Springboks hope actions speak louder than words against Ireland

After a build up to the Ireland Test that has largely been overshadowed by the ban handed down to Rassie Erasmus, there is no doubt the team will be excited to let the rugby do their talking on Saturday.

Mostert, who will earn his 88th Test cap when he takes the field, started on the replacements bench in the games against France and Italy in the last two matches, meaning this will be his third appearance for the team on the November leg of the Nations Championship.

The match kicks off at 18:40 (SA time) and will be broadcast live on SuperSport.

World.title: The best areas to look for cheetahs in Kruger National Park
World.content:
Here's where to find cheetahs in Kruger National Park. Image: canva

Cheetahs are among the most exciting animals to spot on a Kruger National Park safari, but finding one is not always easy.

Unlike lions, which may be seen resting in groups, cheetahs can be difficult to locate in the vast landscape. They favour relatively open habitats where they can scan for prey and use their speed when hunting.

Visitors hoping to see one should focus on the park’s grasslands and open savannah, particularly in the central and southern regions.



1. Satara and the surrounding grasslands

The area around Satara Rest Camp is one of the best-known places to look for cheetahs in Kruger National Park.

The central region has extensive open plains and grassland, which attract grazing animals such as zebra and wildebeest. These provide prey for predators, including cheetahs.

The S100 is one of the roads worth exploring from Satara, while the surrounding routes towards N’wanetsi and Orpen offer further opportunities.



Satara is also known for lion sightings, so visitors may encounter several predators while exploring the area.

2. Orpen and the H7 towards Satara

Orpen Rest Camp is another useful base for visitors interested in cheetah sightings.

SANParks describes the area around Orpen as having wide-open plains and sweet grass that attract browsers and predators.



The H7 between Orpen and Satara is worth including in a self-drive route. It passes through open habitat where cheetahs, lions and other wildlife occur.

The surrounding roads also offer opportunities to see elephants, buffalo, zebra and giraffe.

3. The S28 near Lower Sabie and Crocodile Bridge

The southern part of Kruger also offers opportunities to spot cheetahs.



The S28, which runs through the area between Lower Sabie and Crocodile Bridge, passes through a mix of open grassland and woodland.

The surrounding area includes Nthandanyathi Hide and several waterholes, making it worth exploring slowly.

The roads around Lower Sabie also offer opportunities to see other predators and general game.



4. The open areas around Crocodile Bridge

Crocodile Bridge is another camp worth considering for visitors exploring southern Kruger.

The surrounding region includes open grassland and woodland, with a good variety of prey animals that attract predators.

Visitors can explore the roads around the camp and towards the S28, keeping an eye on open areas and patches of shade where cheetahs may rest.



Cheetah sightings are never guaranteed, but the habitat makes this region worth including in a wider southern Kruger itinerary.

When is the best time to look for cheetahs?

Cheetahs are active during the day, unlike many other predators that are primarily nocturnal.

Early mornings and late afternoons are generally good times to look for them, when temperatures are cooler, and animals may be moving or hunting.



The dry winter months can also improve visibility. Grass is often shorter and vegetation less dense, making it easier to spot animals in open areas.

During the hotter part of the day, cheetahs may rest in the shade or use raised areas such as termite mounds to scan their surroundings.

What should you look for?

Cheetahs are slender cats with long legs, a relatively small head and distinctive black tear marks running from their eyes towards their mouths.



They may be seen resting on termite mounds, low rocky rises or beneath isolated trees.

It is also worth scanning the open ground around herds of impala, wildebeest and zebra, as these are among the animals cheetahs hunt.

Visitors should remain patient and avoid crowding a sighting. Never leave a vehicle to get closer to a cheetah or any other wild animal.



Remember that sightings are never guaranteed

Even in areas known for cheetahs, visitors may drive for hours without seeing one.

The animals move across large territories, and their movements depend on prey, competition with other predators and changing environmental conditions.

A stay near Satara or Orpen may improve your opportunities, but there is no guaranteed route or waterhole where a cheetah will appear.



For the best experience, combine a few promising routes with time to enjoy the rest of Kruger’s wildlife.

World.title: SA crime stats: Western Cape records 80% of gang murders
World.content:
Police and military personnel gather in Cape Town as the latest crime statistics highlight the Western Cape’s high levels of gang-related violence. Image: X/SAFM

The Western Cape accounts for around 80% of South Africa’s gang-related murders and almost 60% of taxi-related killings, according to the latest crime statistics.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia revealed the figures on Friday, 20 November, during the release of the second-quarter crime statistics in Pretoria.

The province also recorded the second-highest risk of murder nationally, behind the Eastern Cape, with KwaZulu-Natal in third place.



Cachalia said the figures showed that violent crime remained concentrated in particular hotspots despite a nationwide decline in murders.

WESTERN CAPE DOMINATES GANG MURDER FIGURES

The Western Cape also recorded 732 murders involving firearms between July and September 2026.

Gauteng recorded 675 firearm-related murders, while KwaZulu-Natal recorded 560.

Nationally, firearms were used in 2 552 murders during the three-month period.

Cachalia warned that the widespread availability of guns continued to fuel gang violence and other serious crimes.

“A firearm turns a dispute into a death,” he said.



He added that firearms enabled gangs and criminal organisations to intimidate communities and increased the danger posed by robberies and targeted attacks.

DELFT AMONG SA’S CRIME HOTSPOTS

The latest figures also placed Delft among the country’s highest-volume police precincts for contact crime.

The Western Cape police station recorded 1 016 contact-crime cases between July and September.

Inanda in KwaZulu-Natal followed with 980 cases.

However, several Western Cape police precincts recorded improvements compared with the same period last year.

Mfuleni registered 222 fewer contact-crime cases, while Nyanga recorded 116 fewer and Khayelitsha 87 fewer.

POLICE TO TARGET GANGS AND ILLEGAL FIREARMS

Cachalia said police would intensify operations against criminal networks, recover illegal firearms and strengthen investigations into organised crime.

He also committed to deploying specialised resources to areas experiencing the highest levels of violence.

Despite a national decline of more than 1 600 murders compared with the same quarter last year, Cachalia warned that South Africa’s murder rate remained far too high.

Police recorded 5 590 murders nationally during the three-month period, averaging approximately 60 killings a day.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates chasing R6.8 million
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates are both in the semi-finals of the Carling Knockout Cup, raising the possibility of another Soweto Derby final.

Both Soweto giants are in action this weekend after avoiding each other in the semi-final draw. This means fans could be treated to a mouthwatering final between the country’s two biggest clubs.

When the Carling Knockout draw was conducted, many fans, except a large section of the Amakhosi faithful, were excited by the prospect of Chiefs facing Mamelodi Sundowns while Pirates were drawn against Stellenbosch FC.



Should both teams win their respective semi-final encounters, football lovers will witness another Soweto Derby in a cup final.

The last time Chiefs and Pirates met in a final was the 2025 Nedbank Cup final, which ended in a 2-1 victory for the Glamour Boys.

However, as much as fans would love to see another showdown between the Soweto rivals, there is no guarantee that either team will make it to the final.



Sundowns go into Sunday’s encounter as favourites against Amakhosi, while Pirates will also have to be wary of a Stellenbosch side with a reputation for causing upsets.

Chiefs and Pirates in action this weekend

Although the Buccaneers might have the edge on paper, Gavin Hunt’s men are more than capable of frustrating the Soweto giants and booking their place in the final.

There is also significant financial motivation, with R6.8 million in prize money up for grabs.



Both Chiefs and Pirates missed out on the R10 million prize after failing to win the MTN8, making the Carling Knockout another opportunity to secure valuable silverware and a substantial financial reward.

For the players, winning the competition would also be an early Christmas present, while supporters would get another reason to celebrate.

Which team will reach the Carling KO final?

World.title: Limpopo records lowest murder rate, Eastern Cape highest
World.content:
PRETORIA - Limpopo has recorded the lowest per-capita murder rate in South Africa, with three murders per 100,000 people.

The Eastern Cape recorded the highest rate, at 16 murders per 100,000 people, followed by the Western Cape at 15 per 100,000.

This is according to the South African Police Service’s (SAPS) crime statistics for the second quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, released on Friday.

A total of 5,590 murders were recorded during the quarter. Of these, 4,819 victims were men, 581 were women and 149 were children. Police said they were able to determine the age and sex of 5,549 victims.

READ | SA records average of 60 murders a day despite decline in violent crime

Arguments and fights were the leading contributors to murders, accounting for 955 cases. Other contributing factors included robbery, retaliation, mob justice and gang-related violence.

The Western Cape accounted for approximately 80% of all gang-related murders and almost 60% of taxi-related murders recorded nationally.

Gauteng recorded the highest number of robbery-related murders.

Liquor outlets, public places and perpetrators’ residences were the three most common locations where murders occurred.

Firearms were used in 2,552 murders during the quarter. The Western Cape recorded the highest number of firearm-related murders, at 732, followed by Gauteng with 675 and KwaZulu-Natal with 560.

Knives were used in 14% of murders, while another 8% involved other sharp instruments.

World.title: Six police officers, three BMA officials arrested for alleged corruption
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Border Management Authority (BMA) has confirmed the arrest of 11 suspects, including three of its officials and six South African Police Service (SAPS) members.

The arrests were made on Friday morning following an investigation into alleged corruption linked to the illegal movement of Lesotho nationals through the Van Rooyen’s Gate Port of Entry between South Africa and Lesotho.

Three Lesotho nationals, identified as alleged facilitators, were arrested before Friday’s operation.

The latest arrests bring the total number of suspects to 11.

An additional SAPS member has also been subpoenaed to appear in court.

World.title: The constant reinvention of Austria's Empress Sisi
World.content:
VIENNA - Visitors flocked from around the world to see a newly redesigned exhibition in Vienna on imperial icon Empress Elisabeth, subject of a string of films and TV series -- and various misunderstandings, according to historians.

Elisabeth, nicknamed Sisi, spent 44 years as empress alongside Franz Joseph I during the final decades of the Habsburg Empire, until her assassination in 1898 by an anarchist during a trip to Geneva.

She has become a global phenomenon over the decades thanks to her portrayals in numerous popular films and shows, including the Netflix series "The Empress".

But historians say the image many people have of her today -- as a romantic, rebellious feminist who railed against the constraints of court life -- bears little resemblance to the woman she actually was.

The Sisi Museum, one of Austria's most popular museums, with 927,000 visitors in 2025, unveiled its new design on Thursday after a multi-year renovation costing 15 million euros ($16 million).

Visitors to the museum can see clothes and shoes that belonged to Sisi, as well as paintings, family mementoes and exercise apparatus representing the empress's famous dedication to fitness.

New attractions include the Weissgoldzimmer (White-Gold Rooms), lavish Rococo rooms that had previously been used as offices by the Austrian chancellery.

Several new objects are also on display, including a highly decorative Boesendorfer grand piano made for Elisabeth, as well as previously unseen dresses, shoes and riding equipment.

- Fairytale heroine -

Museum curator Michael Wohlfahrt said the aim of the redesign was to move beyond the image of Sisi as a larger-than-life cultural icon, with new themes and a wider selection of exhibits that present her "in a completely new environment".

World.title: US auctions first ever deep-sea mining leases, despite court ruling
World.content:
WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump's administration announced it had carried out the nation's first-ever deep-sea mining lease sales off the coast of American Samoa, despite an adverse court ruling earlier this week.

The lease sales cover approximately 12.5 million hectares over two areas off the US Pacific archipelago, and came amid widespread opposition from locals and environmental groups.

Each area sold for $3 million to bidders who have not been identified, for a combined total of $6 million.

"This is the first time the United States has held an offshore critical minerals lease sale in the Pacific and a historic step for America's energy and mineral security," said Interior Secretary Doug Burgum in a statement.

"Today's sale opens a path to learn more about the resources off the coast of American Samoa and assess whether they could contribute to a more reliable domestic supply," he added.

The sale follows an April 2025 executive order in which Trump called leadership in deep-sea science and technology "a core national security and economic interest," and a request by US firm Impossible Metals to open leasing off the territory, which lies east of the independent nation of Samoa.

Mining companies want to scour the ocean's abyssal plains for polymetallic nodules laden with nickel, copper and cobalt -- vital for modern batteries and electric vehicle systems.

Critics fear irreversible damage, with plumes of waste smothering marine life and the thrum of heavy machinery disrupting migrations.

"This premature push to exploit the deep sea before we even fully understand how vital it is will have catastrophic consequences that reverberate for generations," said Oceana Defense Campaign Manager Julia Singer.

American Samoa banned deep-sea mining in its territorial waters in 2024, but the auction concerns the federally controlled Outer Continental Shelf beyond that limit.

In a public comment in September, Governor Pulaali'i Nikolao Pula said he "does not support commercial deep-sea mineral extraction at this time."

On Monday, a federal judge in Hawaii ruled for community and conservation groups, finding that the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) violated the Endangered Species Act when it gave the green light to the sale.

"NMFS failed to even attempt to consider the potential effects on ESA-listed species," Judge Jill Otake wrote.

The lease areas are near the vast Rose Atoll marine sanctuary, home to numerous endangered or threatened species including whales, turtles, sharks and corals.

"In deciding to move forward with today's scheduled sale, the Trump administration has performed a renegade, unlawful act," said Earthjustice attorney Chris Eaton.

"We will use the full extent of the law to vigorously push for the leases to be voided."

World.title: What is El Salvador's Bukele doing in Haiti?
World.content:
SAN SALVADOR - El Salvador's Nayib Bukele has launched a massive military operation in nearby Haiti on the pretext of rescuing four missing soldiers, but the mission's lack of transparency has raised questions about its true aims.

The deployment of over 2,000 troops in Haiti allegedly aims to recover the Salvadoran troops, but the operation's expanding scope is drawing parallels with Bukele's contentious war on gangs at home.

The island nation, the poorest and most violent country in the Americas, has tasked numerous foreign troops with restoring security.

The 2,000-strong United Nations Gang Suppression Force (GSF) has distanced itself from Bukele's recent deployment.

US President Donald Trump backs the operation, although Washington has urged better coordination to avoid friendly fire.

- What have Salvadoran troops done so far? -

In typical bombastic fashion, Bukele has posted dramatic videos on X of helicopters firing on the homes of gang leaders.

One apparently belonged to Jeff Gwo Lwa, a leader of a well-armed gang coalition called Viv Ansanm.

Bukele on Wednesday presented the strike as a "gift" to Haitians, some of whom have marched in support of his operation.

Earlier this month, he announced the destruction of the "headquarters" of the 400 Mawozo gang and residence of leader Wilson Joseph, who was not there.

Last week, Haitian police reported the takeover of a gang-controlled soccer stadium, with Salvadoran and army assistance.

El Salvador's intervention "created a momentum that forces other forces to deliver results," Diego Da Rin, a Haiti specialist at the International Crisis Group, told AFP.

But it has spawned new problems too. Da Rin said gang members have killed alleged operation collaborators and sympathisers.

- What is the scope? -

Bukele insists his troops will leave once they rescue the four soldiers, who disappeared during an ambush by gang members.

On Tuesday, however, El Salvador and Haiti announced a "cooperation agreement" that opens the door to deeper Salvadoran involvement in the long-running crisis.

Neither side has disclosed the details of the agreement, aside from El Salvador saying it funds 90 percent of the operation.

"A military operation... is not discussed publicly. You cannot reveal what the tactics are," said Vice President Felix Ulloa.

Haiti said the agreement opens a "new stage" in facing "security challenges" and on Tuesday, Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier visited El Salvador's "mega-prison" for alleged gang members.

The Salvadorans set up a base in the recovered stadium as a way to push "deeper" into gang-controlled areas, according to Bukele.

That strategy suggested a radical geographical pivot away from the area where the soldiers disappeared, said Da Rin.

El Salvador could be maintaining "ambiguity about the objectives and scope of the deployment because perhaps it is still not clear how financially sustainable it can be," he added.

- What does Bukele want? -

With an approval rating of 80 percent, Bukele's re-election in February is almost guaranteed.

That electoral context deepened doubts about the aim of such an expensive operation in a country where all security strategies have so far failed.

Bukele wants "to cement his image as a hero against organised crime, saying that he not only defeated Salvadoran gangs, but is also helping another country facing a security crisis that seems unsolvable," Da Rin speculated.

"There is an interest in... exporting and selling that model to the world, and this looks like an opportunity to show that off," said Jake Johnston, a US expert on Haiti.

Da Rin noted one significant difference, however.

"These are military operations where the enemy is being killed, not arrested," as in El Salvador, he said.

Amnesty International has warned that Bukele's domestic policies may amount to "crimes against humanity," given reports of arbitrary arrests and deaths and torture in detention.

World.title: Messi tops MLS salaries with Lewandowski next
World.content:
MIAMI - Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in Major League Soccer with $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation, according to a salary release Thursday by the players union, with Chicago's Robert Lewandowski second.

Argentine legend Messi topped the league list revealed by the MLS Players Association with compensation almost $8 million higher than last year, although his figures include only playing compensation and did not include income from other sources.

Messi signed a contract extension through 2028 last year.

Poland's Lewandowski, who joined the Chicago Fire earlier this year, was second overall with $19.51 million followed by Orlando's Antoine Griezmann of France at $13.938 million, South Korean star Son Heung-min of Los Angeles FC at $11.152 million and Swiss international Breel Embolo of Atlanta United at $10.81 million.

Among MLS clubs, Miami topped all teams in total guaranteed compensation at $59.37 million with Chicago second on $41.29 million, Atlanta third on $38.35 million, the Los Angeles Galaxy fourth on $34.91 million and LAFC fifth on $32.91 million.

The league's lowest total team compensation was Philadelphia Union at $12.64 million with Sporting Kansas City second lowest at $13.30 million and DC United third lowest at $14.55 million.

The figures are through October 9 and are annualised for players who arrived in the summer transfer period.

World.title: SA records average of 60 murders a day despite decline in violent crime
World.content:
PRETORIA - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia says that despite a decline in violent crime nationally, levels of violence remain unacceptably high, with an average of 60 people murdered every day between July and September 2026.

The South African Police Service (SAPS) released its crime statistics for the second quarter of the 2026/27 financial year on Friday.

A total of 5,590 murders were recorded between July and September, representing a decrease of more than 1,600 compared with the same period last year.

Cachalia said there had also been notable declines in several categories of violent crime, including armed robberies.

WATCH | Police release latest crime stats

Carjackings fell by 16.8%, while truck hijackings dropped by 27.9%. Robberies at residential and business premises both declined by 7%.

Reported sexual offences also decreased, although by a smaller margin of 2.7%.

“While we have seen reductions in violent crime nationally, and across most provinces, there are some provinces that have recorded increases,” Cachalia said.

According to the minister, the risk of being murdered is highest in the Eastern Cape, followed by the Western Cape and KwaZulu-Natal.

“These figures require a response that is both firm and intelligent. The police must arrest perpetrators, recover weapons, disrupt gangs and bring organised criminals before the courts,” Cachalia said.

World.title: WATCH | Police release latest crime stats
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia and National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola are releasing the second-quarter crime statistics on Friday, covering the period between July and September.

The latest figures are expected to provide an indication of the country's fight against violent crime, as communities continue to grapple with high levels of murder and gun violence.

READ | Stats SA survey paints bleak picture of crime in SA homes

During the previous quarter, more than 5,400 people were murdered across the country, translating to almost 60 killings every day.

The statistics come amid renewed concern over a series of mass shootings, including two separate attacks last weekend that left at least 17 people dead.

With the country facing continued bloodshed, pressure is mounting on the police leadership to demonstrate progress in tackling violent crime and reversing the deadly trend.

World.title: Inside deadly world of landlord tenant feuds
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Cases abound of landlords going to extreme lengths to force tenants to pay, including sealing doors, removing roofs, disconnecting water and electricity, and even hiring goons to intimidate occupants. [File,Standard]

The country recently woke up to shocking news from Kitengela, Kajiado County where a caretaker allegedly struck a tenant with a hammer during a confrontation over a delayed rent balance of Sh1,500.

The caretaker, identified as Shadrack Sanhan Saita, later reported himself to the police and was arrested over the killing of Maurice Otieno Sande in the Noonkopir area.

Sadly, this is far from an isolated case. Every year, extreme landlord-tenant disputes make headlines across the media.

Besides the fatal Kitengela incident, several documented cases show landlords, landladies and their agents resorting to drastic ‘self-help’ measures to force tenants out, particularly when they are unable to pay rent.

Not long ago, a similar incident was reported in Umoja Estate, Nairobi, where a caretaker allegedly stabbed a tenant with a machete following a disagreement over late rent payments. The tenant was seriously injured and hospitalised for several months.

The caretaker fled, while the family, which had lost its breadwinner’s income, relocated to the village. The landlord reportedly distanced himself from the incident, claiming he had not sent the agent to collect rent.

Extreme measures

Cases abound of landlords going to extreme lengths to force tenants to pay, including sealing doors, removing roofs, disconnecting water and electricity, and even hiring goons to intimidate occupants.

In Nakuru, for instance, there was drama at Shaban Estate when a landlord used a welding machine from a nearby garage to seal a tenant’s metallic door over Sh10,000 in rent arrears.

The tenant’s 21-year-old son was trapped inside for six days, communicating with neighbours and journalists through a window until the Deputy County Commissioner intervened.

In Kisumu’s Nyalenda area, a landlady hired a fundi to remove iron sheets over Sh2,400 in arrears, exposing a widow and her three children to heavy rain.

Similar incidents were reported in Thika’s Makongeni Estate over Sh5,000 in arrears and in Nairobi’s Kariobangi Estate after a tenant questioned the landlord over illegal water and electricity connections.

Early this year, a landlord in Kwa Kairu, Ruiru, Kiambu County, sparked outrage after hiring men to dismantle and carry away Ishmael Cheruiyot’s metallic front door over unpaid rent and a deposit balance.

Another incident unfolded in Nairobi’s Kayole Estate, where a landlord removed a tenant’s door and threatened to pour buckets of human waste into the house over rent arrears.

Several cases have also been reported of landlords and their agents padlocking doors from outside, in blatant disregard of legally established procedures for resolving rent disputes.

Behind every incident is a family left scrambling to find shelter.

In Umoja, Grace Omariba, 38, was ordered out of her home with her two children after her landlord had the door dismantled over rent, she was only one week late in paying. She was heavily pregnant at the time, while her husband was at work. Her pleas for more time to raise the money were ignored.

“I had to stay out for several days with my children until we got money to pay rent. That is when the landlord instructed the caretaker to return the door,” she told The Nairobian.

In Komarock, Merceline Awino had lived in her one-bedroom house for almost seven years when her salary was delayed. She asked for more time, but her landlady would hear none of it.

Awino returned from work to find two padlocks on her door and sought refuge at her sister’s home with her three children. “Can you imagine paying your rent promptly for close to a decade and when you develop a problem for one month, you become an enemy with your landlord? Some people can really be inhuman,” she lamented.

In neighbouring Kayole, James Mogere, who had paid rent promptly for nearly five years, was locked out after hospital expenses for a sick relative delayed his payment. His belongings were thrown onto the veranda.

With no means of renting another house, the family had to split up: his wife and three children went to live with her sister, while he sought shelter with a friend.

What the law says

Kenyan law is clear that such actions are not lawful. Under the Penal Code, the Distress for Rent Act (Cap 293) and the Rent Restriction Act (Cap 296), landlords cannot resort to forceful measures, such as welding doors shut, removing roofs or cutting off essential services to compel tenants to vacate.

Even where a tenant owes rent, a landlord must follow the prescribed legal procedures before eviction. These include issuing the required formal notice and obtaining the necessary tribunal or court orders. Any seizure of a tenant’s property must also follow the law, including the use of a licensed auctioneer where required.

Section 29 of the Rent Restriction Act makes it a criminal offence to wilfully subject a tenant to annoyance, including removing windows, doors or taps, or disconnecting water and electricity to force them out.

The offence carries a penalty of up to six months’ imprisonment and may also attract charges under the Penal Code for malicious damage to property or criminal trespass, depending on the circumstances.

Advocate William Onyonje of Onyonje & Co Advocates says the legal route for resolving tenancy disputes is well established. “The best way for landlords to deal with a tenant who has defaulted is by first sending a notice to serve as a reminder to the tenant to make good their dues,” he says.

“If that fails, he or she can take the dispute to one of the two distinct tribunals: the Rent Restriction Tribunal for ordinary residential tenancies, or the Business Premises Rent Tribunal for catering, hotels and other business tenancies,” he adds.

Onyonje explains that the two tribunals are mandated to resolve landlord-tenant disputes and grant relief to either party. They consider whether the tenant has paid the rent due and whether the landlord has provided vacant and peaceful possession.

Depending on their findings, a tribunal may order a defaulting tenant to clear outstanding rent and vacate, while a landlord may be authorised to levy distress for rent under the Distress for Rent Act.

Onyonje urges both parties to exercise patience and follow the prescribed procedures, saying this helps resolve disputes while preserving good relations in the long run.

Illegal evictions punished

Kenyan courts have consistently penalised landlords who take the law into their own hands.

In Wambugu vs Njoroge, the High Court awarded a tenant Sh300,000 in general damages after the landlord carried out an unlawful eviction and seized property without proper notice.

In Arege vs Michira (2024), the Environment and Land Court dealt with the unlawful eviction of Daniel Boit Arege, a hotel operator in Kisii. The landlord, Alfred Moffat Omundi Michira, had evicted him on May 13, 2017, without following the required legal procedures.

The landlord also seized the tenant’s business property despite existing tribunal orders restraining the eviction. The court awarded Sh240,000 in general damages for unlawful eviction and Sh200,000 for goods retained by the landlord. It further declared the eviction illegal, wrongful and void from the beginning.

In Wambugu & another v City Council of Nairobi (2023), the case involved Jacob Kioi Wambugu and Shelmith Gathoni Wambugu, who had occupied a Nairobi City Council house along Outer Ring Road Estate since 1970.

The council forcibly evicted the family on April 13, 1988, without issuing a written termination notice. During the eviction, the tenants’ belongings were thrown out, children were reportedly beaten and their parents detained.

The Environment and Land Court found the eviction unlawful and awarded a total of Sh25.3 million, comprising Sh15 million in exemplary damages, Sh8.3 million in special damages and Sh2 million in general damages.

Association condemns killing

Amid the latest incident in Kitengela, which left many people shocked, the Landlords and Tenants Association of Kenya (LATAK) has condemned the killing of Otieno, describing it as a tragic consequence of a tenancy dispute that turned violent.

LATAK Secretary-General Ben Liyai stressed that no rent arrears, regardless of the amount involved, could ever justify taking someone’s life. “Human life is sacred, and disagreements over rent must never degenerate into violence. The landlord-tenant relationship must rest on responsibility, mutual respect and the rule of law,” he said.

Tenants, he noted, are obliged to pay rent as agreed, while landlords and their agents must respect tenants’ rights and dignity.

“Rent disputes are civil matters that should be handled through established legal channels, and landlords and property managers must never use intimidation, threats or violence to recover arrears,” he advised.

Tenant obligations

He was equally firm that tenants had obligations of their own, including honouring contractual agreements, communicating transparently when facing financial difficulties and respecting the legitimate interests of property owners.

Liyai said the Kitengela tragedy underscored the urgent need for greater awareness of landlord and tenant rights and responsibilities, proper training for property agents and caretakers, and accessible mechanisms for resolving tenancy disputes.

“LATAK advocates for a balanced rental housing environment where the rights of both landlords and tenants are protected. We believe that justice, dialogue and the rule of law must always prevail,” he said.

From a Sh1,500 debt that ended in a killing to families locked out, left roofless or forced apart over delayed rent, the cases point to the same conclusion: the law already provides a framework for resolving tenancy disputes, and it does not involve a hammer, padlock, welding machine or blade.

For landlords, the lawful course is to issue notice and pursue the appropriate tribunal or court process. For tenants, it is to communicate early and understand their rights. For both parties, the alternative has proved far too costly.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.
