World.title: Malaysia carnival brings food, culture and travel experiences to Jeddah
World.content:
JEDDAH: Malaysian cuisine, traditional performances and travel experiences brought a taste of Southeast Asia to Jeddah as the two-day Malaysia Carnival 2026–2027 opened at Cenomi U-Walk Mall on Thursday.

Held on Nov. 19 and 20, the carnival featured live cooking demonstrations of popular dishes such as satay and nasi lemak, traditional music and dance performances, and demonstrations of teh tarik, Malaysia’s traditional pulled milk tea. Tourism representatives also presented holiday packages, hotels and family destinations.

Visitors explored Malaysian products, educational opportunities and healthcare services, offering a glimpse of the country’s wider tourism and lifestyle offerings.

My Makan KSA, which is participating in its second year of operations in Saudi Arabia, is presenting Malaysian cuisine alongside products imported from small and medium-sized businesses in Malaysia.

The opening ceremony was attended by Fareed bin Saad Al-Shehri, director general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs branch in the Makkah region, alongside Zaidi Kassim, director of Tourism Malaysia Jeddah. (Supplied)

“The idea is to bring Malaysian food and products together under one roof, giving visitors an opportunity to discover what we eat and what Malaysia produces. The carnival is an ideal platform to introduce our culture and traditions and raise awareness of Malaysian food in Saudi Arabia,” Mohammed Fakhrul Razi, the company’s CEO, told Arab News.

Education Malaysia Global Assist is using the event to reach out to students and families interested in pursuing higher education in Malaysia, introducing its university network and student placement services.

“We want to connect with students and families, explain the universities and courses available, and guide them through the admission process. We also help students identify institutions that match their budgets and preferences, as well as scholarships they may be eligible for,” said Wani Hanisah, the organization’s manager of student placement.

Visitors explored Malaysian products, educational opportunities and healthcare services, offering a glimpse of the country's wider tourism and lifestyle offerings. (Supplied)

Representing Malaysian universities, including private institutions and international branch campuses, the organization has offices in Jeddah and Dammam. Hanisah said approximately 300 students from Saudi Arabia enrolled in Malaysian universities between January and September this year.

She attributed the interest partly to the affordability of education in Malaysia and expressed hope that more students would consider the country for their higher education.

For Malaysian resident Fayez Mohammed, the celebrations brought back memories of home.

“I felt as though I was back in Malaysia. I enjoyed the food, the dance performances and seeing people asking questions about our culture. Since it was held in a mall, families could easily stop by and enjoy the celebrations. It is good that the event is introducing the country and its traditions to more people,” he said.

Visitors explored Malaysian products, educational opportunities and healthcare services, offering a glimpse of the country's wider tourism and lifestyle offerings. (Supplied)

Adnan Al-Hussein, who visited the mall with his family, said they had come for shopping but decided to explore the carnival after noticing the celebrations.

“It was very vibrant, and we were welcomed at the entrance by people wearing colorful traditional clothes. We enjoyed the cultural performances and the food stalls. It is good to see activities like this taking place in Jeddah,” he said.

The carnival formed part of the wider Visit Malaysia 2026–2027 campaign, which aims to increase international visitor numbers and tourism revenue. Saudi Arabia is an important market for Malaysia, with the country offering attractions ranging from shopping and nature-based experiences to halal dining, prayer facilities and family tourism.

Visitors explored Malaysian products, educational opportunities and healthcare services, offering a glimpse of the country's wider tourism and lifestyle offerings. (Supplied)

At the opening ceremony, Malaysia’s Consul General in Jeddah, Tengku Datuk Mohd Dzaraif Raja Abdul Kadir said, “Malaysia offers visitors a rich mix of colorful culture, authentic cuisine and diverse travel experiences. We want Saudi visitors to see Malaysia as their second home, with opportunities to explore not only its tourism attractions but also its education and investment sectors.”

The opening ceremony was attended by Fareed bin Saad Al-Shehri, director-general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs branch in the Makkah region, alongside Zaidi Kassim, director of Tourism Malaysia Jeddah. Consuls general and diplomatic representatives from ASEAN member states Oman and India were also present.

World.title: Jordan eyes green economy to drive investment and job creation
World.content:
DEAD SEA: Jordan is seeking to attract fresh investment into its renewable energy sector, as it looks to build on a decade of clean-energy growth and develop new industries such as green hydrogen and ammonia.

Renewables now account for more than a quarter of the Kingdom’s electricity mix, but officials and industry representatives say further investment in solar, wind and energy storage will be needed to sustain that progress and strengthen energy security.

The push was a key focus of the Jordan-EU Investment Summit at the Dead Sea, where government officials, European institutions and private-sector representatives explored opportunities to finance the Kingdom’s green transition.

Beyond generating electricity, Jordan wants to use its renewable resources to develop new industries.

In Aqaba, a planned $1 billion green ammonia facility could turn solar power into a product for international markets, opening up opportunities in the emerging green fuels industry.

Shada El-Sharif‏, founder and CEO of SustainMENA told Arab News that Jordan has already taken the steps towards transitioning into a green economy.

The country's Economic Modernisation Vision, launched in 2022, identified such a development as one of its eight economic drivers, explained El-Sharif.

“Renewables currently account for 27 percent of Jordan's electricity mix, a milestone achieved in just over a decade. Additionally, 21 percent of vehicles in the country are either hybrid or electric,” she said.

“The vision has an ambitious target of unlocking JD41 billion Jordanian dinars ($57.9 billion) in investment by 2033 and creating 1 million jobs. We believe the green economy can deliver a substantial share of that investment and employment,” explained El-Sharif.

Shada El-Sharif‏, founder and CEO of SustainMENA

SustainMENA, an advisory organisation operates across the Middle East and North Africa and focuses on supporting organisations in the public, private and international sectors with the green transition.

“Our work includes advising on the policies required to advance the transition, developing projects, conducting feasibility studies and raising awareness. Awareness is particularly important because it plays a major role in encouraging the adoption of a green economy across our region,” explained the CEO.

El-Sharif said stability in the region is essential towards speeding up the pace of investments into the green and digital economy, but assured that Jordan’s proven resilience positions it as a key opportunity for investment.

“Clear regulations are also essential. Jordan has established regulatory frameworks for renewable energy, waste and transport, alongside a new electricity law that promotes emerging technologies such as green hydrogen and energy storage,” she added.

World.title: Rare Al-Batalyawsi manuscript unveiled by KFCRIS
World.content:
RIYADH: A unique manuscript copy of “Ithbat Al-Nubuwwat” (“Proof of Prophethood”) by Andalusian philosopher and linguist Ibn Al-Sid Al-Batalyawsi has been discovered by the King Faisal Center for Research and Islamic Studies.

The unveiling of the text, which was considered lost for centuries, coincides with the launch of the Arabic Philosophy Studies Program, marking World Philosophy Day.

The discovery comes as part of the center’s efforts to revive Arab and Islamic heritage and highlight its intellectual contributions. The manuscript is the only known surviving copy of the book to date and was copied by Mohammed ibn Abdullah ibn Abd Al-Salam Al-Sudafi in around 1229 in a partially vocalized Andalusian script. Most of its text remains legible despite damage to some sections over time.

A unique manuscript copy of the book “Ithbat Al-Nubuwwat.” (Akhbaar 24)

The book is of particular significance for its philosophical and theological discussions of the possibility and truth of prophethood. Its author draws on rational arguments to examine differing views, presents responses to those who deny prophethood, and discusses the claim that it is a product of imagination. He also explores the visions experienced by prophets and the distinctions between a prophet, a sorcerer and a soothsayer.

It also reviews the views of several Greek and Islamic philosophers, allowing researchers to Al-Batalyawsi’s intellectual sources, analyze his approach to constructing arguments and addressing objections, and understand his perspective on the relationship between reason and revelation, and philosophy and religion.

The book’s title has been preserved in biographical works. Al-Firuzabadi listed it among Al-Batalyawsi’s works in his book “Al-Bulghah fi Tarajim A’immat Al-Nahw wa Al-Lughah” (“Summary of the Biographies of the Imams of Grammar and Language”.) The discovery of the manuscript allows researchers to move beyond merely knowing the title of the work to studying its text and analyzing its ideas.

The Arabic Philosophy Studies Program aims to study, uncover, critically edit and critique Arabic philosophical texts dating from around the eighth to 16th centuries, with particular attention to the development of philosophical terminology and concepts and the transmission of ideas across cultures and languages.

In partnership with the KFCRIS Arabic Book Chair, the program is set to undertake a critical edition of “Ithbat Al-Nubuwwat” and publish it in a scholarly edition accompanied by a specialized study during an academic symposium that the center plans to organize in November 2027. The event will introduce the author, examine the context in which the book was written, describe the manuscript, analyze its content and sources, and compare it with his other works.

KFCRIS has also announced it will dedicate 2027 to celebrating Al-Batalyawsi’s legacy, marking the 900th anniversary of his death according to the Gregorian calendar. It invited researchers, universities and research centers to participate through academic studies and symposia, and to support efforts to publish his works and highlight his contributions to philosophy and Arabic linguistics.

The initiatives include preparing a bibliographical study of his writings, documenting their manuscripts, published editions and works that remain lost, as well as compiling studies and research related to him. They also include translating into Arabic a study by Spanish researcher Salvador Pena Martín titled “The Quran, the Word and Truth: Ibn Al-Sid and Humanism in Al-Andalus.”

The symposium will also be accompanied by an exhibition, Masterpieces of Andalusian Manuscript Heritage, which will highlight selected Andalusian manuscripts and provide information on when they were copied, their scripts and their scholarly value. It will also explore the relationship between language and logic in Al-Batalyawsi’s writings, his views on questions of prophethood, reason and revelation, and the presence of his works in Hebrew and Spanish studies.

Al-Batalyawsi, who lived from 1052 to 1127 CE, is regarded as one of the most prominent philosophers and linguists of Al-Andalus. He lived through the final years of the Taifa kingdoms and the period of Almoravid rule, settled in Valencia, and engaged in scholarly debates with the philosopher Ibn Bajjah, some of which were preserved in his book “Al-Masa’il wa Al-Ajwibah” (“Questions and Answers”.)

KFCRIS previously demonstrated interest in his intellectual legacy by publishing “Rasa’il fi Al-Lughah” (“Treatises on Language”) in 2007. The book, which comprised 18 treatises, was published as part of its critical heritage edition series edited by Dr. Walid Muhammad Al-Sarraqbi. The discovery of the Al-Nubuwwat manuscript builds on this longstanding interest and opens up a new avenue for studying the philosophical dimension of his intellectual output.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, offers condolences over mother's death
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to

chief minister

and expressed condolences over the death of his mother,

, who passed away at the age of 91 in her native village in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district.

Savitri Devi died around 10.45 am on Friday in Panchur village, residents told PTI. She had been unwell for a long time and could recognise only family members, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha said.

Pauri Garhwal Senior Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Panwar said the local administration was in touch with the family.

Adityanath was attending a public function in Uttar Pradesh when he received the news of his mother's death.



He had two more official engagements scheduled for later in the day and was expected to continue with his programme. It was not immediately clear whether he would travel to Uttarakhand for the last rites, which are likely to be held on Saturday.

G C Badola, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha, told PTI, âOne of her sons is posted in Kotdwar and will reach the village by Friday evening. The last rites will likely be conducted at Phool Chatti Ghat near the village on Saturday, where the last rites of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanathâs father were also held.â





Defence minister Rajnath Singh expressed grief over Savitri Devi's death in a post on X, saying the loss of a mother was one of the most unbearable blows in life. He extended his condolences to Adityanath and his family.

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also described her death as extremely sad and heartbreaking, saying, "Her demise is an irreparable loss to the family." He extended his condolences to the bereaved family and prayed for strength for them to cope with the loss.

Adityanath's father, Anand Singh Bisht, died following a prolonged illness in 2020. His last rites were performed in Uttarakhand. Adityanath did not attend the funeral due to the Covid-19 lockdown and his responsibilities as Uttar Pradesh chief minister.

World.title: 'Rubbing salt into Pahalgam victims' wounds': Row over Pakistan minister at SCO meet in Delhi
World.content:
Congress leaders criticised the Centre over Pakistan minister Masood Malik's visit to Delhi for the SCO Civilisation Dialogue

th

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A political row broke out after Pakistan minister Masood Malik arrived in Delhi on Friday to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. Congress questioned the invitation and accused the BJP-led Centre of ârubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victimsâ familiesâ."You keep changing your stance. Sometimes you travel there, sometimes you reach Lahore, at other times you abruptly call off Operation Sindoor, and now you invite them here. What exactly is Prime Minister Modi doing? The funeral pyres of those martyred in the Pahalgam massacre have not even cooled yet, and you are rubbing salt into the wounds of their families,â said Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate."The Government of India, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is organising the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India on November 21 and 22. The question is: why was Pakistan invited to this event? Why have you invited Pakistan, a country that sponsors terrorism in India? You invited Pakistan, and its minister, Musadik Malik, has arrived here," she said.Questioning the "red carpet" treatment being extended to the minister, Shrinate said, "This is the same person who had openly threatened just a few months ago to chop off the hands of Indians and shed our blood.""The question is that Pakistan has not stopped sponsoring terrorism, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is busy welcoming its representatives. Musadik Malik be served biryani, kebabs and kheer? The government is rolling out the red carpet to welcome him. Why does your work not get done without an anti-India Pakistan? The point is that you should also say and do what Rahul Gandhi has stated unequivocally: as long as Pakistan continues to sponsor terrorism, no dialogue with it is possible," she added.J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra also accused the BJP of having "double standards" regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties."Look, as far as the Government of India is concerned, particularly the BJP,ey have always had double standards. Whether it is regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties, their approach has consistently been marked by double standards. The very person who made the loudest protests when the Indus Waters Treaty was suspended here had raised more objections than anyone else at that time. But the fact that they are displaying double standards is nothing new," he said."This is another example of their double standards. When our Prime Minister went to Pakistan uninvited, what could be a bigger example of double standards than that? Basically, the BJP has lost its track.Its foreign policy is being handled on a day-to-day basis. It has no consistent or permanent policy towards its neighbouring countries, whether Pakistan, China, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka. They deal with each country according to what suits them at a particular time," he added.Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. He was received by Pakistan high commissioner's ChargÃ© d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich. Malik's visit marks the first time a Pakistani minister has travelled to India in three years.

World.title: Hunger has no caste, creed or colour: Aruna Lohia Goenka on the power of anna
World.content:
For three decades, impact catalyst

Aruna Lohia Goenka

has followed one remarkably simple instinct across homes, classrooms, hospitals, communities and public institutions: when someone needs help, do something. In this edition of the knowledge series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, explores

Anna

(nourishment) - one of the five pillars of her YASHA framework for

Viksit Bharat 2047

, alongside Shiksha (education), Yuva (youth), Hunar (skills) and Abundance (shared prosperity).

Sanjiv Kaura:

When my team researched your work, we discovered perhaps the world's most unusual restaurant - your langar.

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

(Laughs) Well, Sanjiv, we certainly haven't had a âreservations deskâ in our langar for the last 3 decades! The reason is simple: hunger doesn't make appointments

.

Anyone can come to my home and receive food. No application. No appointment. No eligibility test! To me, it is one of the most natural and satisfying things to do.

Sanjiv Kaura:

You have experienced wealth and yet you say that your langar gives you a satisfaction no amount of wealth can buy. Isn't this a paradox?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Only if we assume that everything valuable has a price! (Laughs). A meal has a price. A blessing doesn't come with a price tag! Sanjiv, I don't really think of myself as giving anything.

I am simply sharing my abundance. Service comes naturally to me. It is my joy. That is why I often say to myself: Feed. Feed. Feed.

Sanjiv Kaura:

You make feeding sound almost spiritual. Is that why Annapurna resonates so strongly with your philosophy?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Annapurna represents something beautiful in our tradition - the assurance that nobody should remain hungry. To me, that also means responsibility. If the Universe has been generous to us, surely, we can share that abundance with others?

Take a hospital, for example. While doctors care for patients, who looks after their families? That is what led me to become involved in pioneering community kitchens serving patients' families outside AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences), New Delhi.

Sanjiv Kaura:

And how did water become part of your mission?

Aruna Lohia Goenka

: (Laughs) Sanjiv, when someone is thirsty in 45-degree heat, they don't need a lecture on climate change. They need a glass of cool water!

When the Delhi Heat Action Plan was launched by the Chief Minister. Rekha Gupta, I was delighted to be invited by Rajendra Singh of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to support the initiative through digital cool-water dispensing machines. Impact doesn't have to be glamorous. It has to be useful!

Sanjiv Kaura:

Could your philosophy of

âEach One, Feed Oneâ

help bridge the rural -urban divide?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Absolutely! The people constructing and maintaining our homes and cities often come from distant villages.

The hands that build our prosperity deserve a generous share of that prosperity.

As fellow Bharatwasis, isn't it our responsibility to ensure that they receive fresh, nutritious food, are paid generously for their services and are treated with dignity?

And I mean proper nutrition - wholesome, preferably home-cooked food prepared with good ingredients and healthy oils.

Think of a migrant worker who has come to a city to earn a livelihood but has no kitchen of his own.

If we provide him with fresh, nutritious food, he not only stays healthier but can also save more of his hard-earned income. And where do those savings go? Back to his family in the village! That money flows into rural Bharat, supporting families, strengthening local businesses and, as it circulates through village economies, potentially contributing to better housing, facilities and infrastructure.

The possibilities - 400 cities impacting 16,000 villages

Our cities have infrastructure that many of our villages still lack. What if we could help bridge that gap through something as simple as sharing nutritious food? Every migrant worker is a human bridge between rural and urban Bharat. If we strengthen that bridge, we strengthen Bharat itself!

And Sanjiv, life is a mirror. When we help others grow, we grow too.

Their prosperity is our prosperity.

That is why I believe

âEach One, Feed Oneâ

can become something much larger than a meal.

Sanjiv Kaura:

That sounds like a much bigger idea than feeding people. Are you suggesting that Anna is also about how we treat one another?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Precisely! Anna begins with food, but it cannot end there. What good is a meal if we deny someone dignity? We must recognise that the people who serve us are our fellow Bharatiyas. Their nutrition, welfare and dignity should matter to us. Pay them generously. Feed them nutritiously. Treat them respectfully, with dignity

.

I find the thinking of Nobel Laureate and Harvard University Professor Amartya Sen particularly profound: development is not merely about rising incomes, but about expanding people's real freedoms - including the freedom to live without hunger. After all, what meaning does prosperity have if people are still denied the basic dignity of a nutritious meal?

Sanjiv Kaura:

But isn't hunger fundamentally the government's responsibility?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

A government can create a food-security system. Citizens help create a culture in which nobody's hunger is ignored. I believe that caring for our fellow citizens is a personal responsibility, not merely an act of generosity. It is a moral commitment. That is the Bharat I would love to see. I believe we need to rediscover a very personal relationship with our country. Every morning, why not ask ourselves one little question: What can I do today to make my Bharat a little better?

Sanjiv Kaura:

But how do we turn that sentiment into something practical?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

(Laughs) Ah, Sanjiv! We Bharatiyas are very good at slogans. Sometimes we need to be equally good at acting upon them!

Let us start with a small deed, not a big program:

Perhaps I cannot feed a thousand people. Can I feed one?

Perhaps I cannot transform an entire village. Can I help one family?

Perhaps I cannot solve every problem. Can I at least stop walking past one?

Each one, feed one!

Sanjiv Kaura:

Finally, how does Anna fit into your larger vision of Viksit Bharat 2047?

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Sanjiv, along with economic growth, technology and global influence, we must nourish our workers and our future generations.

A well-nourished Bharat is the foundation of a Viksit Bharat.

I have always loved the writings of Ralph Waldo Emerson. One thought I draw from his philosophy is that when we hold a powerful vision and act upon it with conviction, the world around us can begin to move in that direction. I believe that when we send a thought of goodness into the Universe, and follow it with action, we help make that goodness a reality. I dream of a healthy nation.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Four hundred cities. Sixteen thousand villages.

Millions of lives touched by one simple idea: Each One, Feed One! That is my dream for Bharat. And Sanjiv, I can see it happening!

You may possess the Kohinoor, but what good will it do you when it cannot give you a blessing? Feed a hungry person, and you will definitely receive a blessing that no diamond can ever give.

(Laughs) So my message is simple: Live consciously. Look beyond yourself. Each one, feed one.

World.title: Pakistan analyst claims no Indian official welcomed Musadik Malik in Delhi; fact-checked
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A claim by Pakistani think tank analyst that no Indian official was present to receive Pakistan's minister Musadik Masood Malik, upon his arrival in New Delhi has been contradicted by official sources cited by news agency ANI.

Khurram Abbas alleged that India had not extended the customary official welcome to Malik, who arrived in the national capital on Thursday to attend the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum.

"India didnât show courtesy to send official to welcome Pakistan climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Malik who arrived in Delhi to attend SCO meeting. He was welcomed by the Pakistani CdA.



First Pakistan minister in India since 2023 & May 2025 conflict," Abbas alleged in a post on X.

However, according to sources cited by news agency ANI, a director from the Union ministry of culture and an under secretary from the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the MEA were present at the airport to receive Malik as part of the welcome protocol.

The sources also clarified that all SCO member countries arriving in New Delhi were being extended a similar level of protocol.





Malik's visit is significant as he is the first Pakistani minister to travel to India in three years and the first since the May 2025 military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed countries following the

, in which 26 people were killed by Pakistan-backed terrorists in

.

The last high-profile visit by a Pakistani political leader was that of then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari in 2023.

Why is the Pakistani minister visiting India

Malik is in New Delhi to participate in the thematic sessions of the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, scheduled to be held from November 20 to 22.

According to Pakistan's ministry of foreign affairs, Malik will represent Islamabad at the forum and present Pakistan's perspective on the importance of dialogue among civilisations and its role in diplomacy.

In a statement, the ministry said the minister's address would highlight Pakistan's constructive role in the SCO, along with the country's diverse civilisational and cultural heritage.

"Pakistan's participation in this Forum is reflective of its contribution as an active State to promote dialogue, cooperation and understanding in line with the 'Shanghai Spirit'," the statement said.

Pakistan's participation follows India's invitation to all 10 SCO member states, along with observer countries and dialogue partners, to attend the inaugural forum.

The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had earlier confirmed that several countries, including SCO member states, had been invited to the event, adding that New Delhi looked forward to hosting the dialogue.

Proposed by India, the initiative aims to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties across the Eurasian region.

Defence minister Rajnath Singh had announced India's plan to host the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20.

The SCO has 10 member states, including India, Pakistan, China and Russia. India became a full member of the grouping in 2017.

World.title: SC upholds Karnataka HC order to allow bike taxis, rejects state govt's challenge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a setback to the Karnataka government, the

on Friday refused to interfere with a state high court ruling that permits bike taxi services to operate across Karnataka.

A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the state's appeal, thereby retaining the relief granted to bike taxi aggregators and operators by the Karnataka High Court, news agency ANI reported.

The case dates back to an earlier order that had asked bike taxi operators to halt services until the state introduced a regulatory framework. However, on January 23, 2026, a division bench of the high court, then headed by Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and comprising Justice CM Joshi, overturned that direction.



The high court's ruling came on appeals by

, Uber, Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. It said motorcycles could be registered as transport vehicles and used as contract carriages, provided they complied with the state's regulatory requirements.

World.title: Karthigai Deepam row: SC allows one-time lamp lighting atop Thiruparankundram hill on November 24
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has permitted the lighting of the traditional

lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on November 24, 2026, as an interim arrangement.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, however, stayed portions of the

judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon. The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah over ownership of the hilltop and the location of the ritual.

The development follows arguments by the dargah before the top court on Thursday, when it claimed ownership of the entire hilltop and opposed the demand to light the lamp at the stone pillar.



The hearing on the matter had remained inconclusive, with the court scheduled to continue proceedings on Friday.

Senior advocate Amit Anand Tiwari, appearing for the dargah, referred to a 1920 judicial order passed in a civil suit and said there were findings establishing that the flight of stairs from Nellithope to the hill belonged to the shrine.

"The entire top of the hill belongs to the dargah. There is no question of lighting the deepam at the top of the hill, where the stone pillar is situated, irrespective of what the distance between the dargah and the stone pillar is," Tiwari said.





He also submitted that the "whole of the top of the hillock on which the mosque and the flagstaff stand" as well as the stone pillar are located is the property of the dargah.

What is the Karthigai Deepam dispute

The controversy centres on the location of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lighting ceremony at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Thiruparankundram. For decades, the festival lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of the hill.

Hindu groups have sought permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the dargah. The dispute has led to legal proceedings over the location of the ritual and ownership of the hill.

The Tamil Nadu government had opposed the demand, arguing that permitting the lighting of the lamp near the dargah could create wider legal and administrative complications.

On Wednesday, it told the Supreme Court that allowing the practice could lead to thousands of survey pillars across the country acquiring a religious character.

The dargah committee had also challenged the procedure followed by the Madras High Court. Senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi, appearing for the committee, argued that a single-judge bench had passed its order without giving the dargah adequate time to file a reply under the high court rules.

He also submitted that the judge had conducted a site visit without notifying the dargah before passing the order.

Tamil Nadu government opposes ASI takeover

The Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department has opposed a petition seeking to bring the temple and the entire Thiruparankundram hill under the control of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

In an affidavit before the Supreme Court, HR&CE Commissioner T G Vinay said the temple's ownership and existing religious practices had been settled through decades of judicial proceedings.

He maintained that the hill was owned by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple to the extent recognised by a civil court decree of 1923, which was subsequently restored by the Privy Council in 1931.

The affidavit opposed three reliefs sought by petitioner Hindu Dharma Parishad: handing over the entire temple and hill to the ASI, keeping a lamp burning round the clock at the stone pillar described as the Deepathoon, and illuminating the entire hill with lamps during Karthigai Deepam.

"A title so settled cannot be disturbed and the administration of a religious endowment entrusted by statute to the HR&CE cannot be wrested away and handed over to the ASI upon a petition that pleads no ground in law and seeks the relief in the teeth of a concluded civil adjudication of title," the affidavit had said.

On the lighting ceremony, the HR&CE commissioner maintained that the festival lamp had traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple, and not at the hilltop or the stone pillar.

The department also referred to historical records of attempts made in 1862 and 1912 to light lamps near the hill's summit, where the dargah is situated. It argued that archaeological protection at Thiruparankundram covered specified features, including the rock-cut cave and inscriptions, and did not extend to the entire hill or the functioning temple.

The department cautioned that allowing lamps to be lit at multiple locations, particularly near the dargah, could disrupt existing arrangements and create law-and-order challenges at a site with a history of communal tension.

World.title: Operation Monsoon Thunder:  NCB raids four cities, arrests six in probe into US-bound opioid and psychotropic drug shipments
World.content:
Arti Soni, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh/ Abdul Muttalib @ Rocky @ Monio Kolkata, West Bengal/ Talabathula Manoj Allapur, Hyderabad

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: In a sweeping international crackdown, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have dismantled the Indian nerve center of a massive transnational drug syndicate â shutting down an illicit pipeline flooding American streets with deadly opioids and psychotropic substances.âUnder an operation code named, Monsoon Thunder, NCB teams carried out raids across multiple Indian cities âincluding Hyderabad, Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow â resulting in the arrest of six individuals linked to the network.The raids were carried on Nov 4 and Nov 13. According to investigative findings, the syndicate operated across borders to supply controlled drugs to buyers throughout the United States.Digital records and examined evidence indicate that the group handled nearly 3,000 parcels containing approximately five lakh tablets between June 2022 and November 2026.During the probe, NCB also flagged several active consignments holding more than 1,500 tablets bound for U.S. destinations and shared actionable intelligence with the DEA, which subsequently seized two shipment consignments.Investigators found that Indian operators took orders via encrypted and messaging platforms such as Telegram, Skype, and WhatsApp, while the U.S.-based arm dispatched shipments through postal and delivery networks, including the United States Postal Service (USPS).Consignment and buyer information was tracked in shared digital records, including Google Sheets. Authorities uncovered a vast customer database covering more than 59,000 subjectsâcontaining transaction histories, past shipment details, delivery addresses, USPS tracking IDs, and drug typesâwhich has been handed over to the DEA to support ongoing intelligence analysis and enforcement against U.S. buyers and drop-shippers.Financial probes show that Indian operators collected payments and commissions through multiple channels, including Venmo, UPI, cryptocurrency, third-party bank accounts, and hawala networks.Investigators are tracing these financial flows to identify ultimate beneficiaries and map illicit proceeds. Additionally, digital files and medicine brand details recovered from an arrested operative point to potential sourcing from several countries, prompting further investigation into procurement channels and international movement.NCB officials said the operation highlights ongoing efforts to counter syndicates abusing digital tools, postal systems, and cross-border supply chains for illicit pharmaceutical trafficking, reaffirming commitment to coordinated international enforcement against narcotic and psychotropic drug networks.

World.title: SpiceJet cash crunch hits flight operations; Delhi airport issues advisory for flyers
World.content:
Delhi airport flags possible flight disruptions over SpiceJet's âoperational challengesâ
