Samoa have won each of their previous two matches against Spain, including a 34-30 victory in their most recent meeting in 2024.

Meanwhile, Spain will look to bounce back from last weekend's 25-20 defeat to Chile.

Changes to their pack see prop Raul Calzon earning a start, while Alex Saleta Atorrasagasti and Mateo Triki replace Gabriel Velez and Matthew Foulds as the starting flankers.

Nicolas Infer and Gonzalo Lopez form a new halfback combination, the former making his first start for Los Leones, while centre Alvar Gimeno and winger Gauthier Minguillon also come into the backline.

World.title: Nursing graduates turn to other industries, after struggling for jobs in medicine
World.content:
Newly graduated enrolled nurses say a lack of jobs is forcing them to work on building sites and in bars to make ends meet.

An enrolled nursing diploma takes 18 months, half the time of a bachelor's degree to become a registered nurse, but it gives graduates the scope to care for patients, record vitals, and administer medication across public and private healthcare.

Yet, despite ongoing reports of chronic understaffing, graduates say getting a foot in the door has become nearly impossible.

Enrolled nurse Shelley Slater has traded medical scrubs and shift work in the wards for a toolbelt and a building site, as she hasn't been able to find work.

She graduated from Taranaki's Western Institute of Technology at the beginning of this year.

Audio player for " Graduate Enrolled Nurses stilll struggling to find work " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._v0.KrRTFtoPsaA8nSDloPZ4KejQJr59ANQpD9ULgGwzaM0/health/2710266%2Fnursing-graduates-turn-to-other-industries-after-struggling-for-jobs-in-medicine

Graduate Enrolled Nurses stilll struggling to find work Checkpoint Download MP3 4m

After applying for work through Health New Zealand's graduate nursing portal, and for dozens of jobs across aged care and the private sector, she felt like she had hit a wall.

"I had to stop [applying] physically, mentally during the year," Slater said. "My family just said this is ridiculous, it's just enough.

"[They said] good on you, you've done this thing and it's great, but [applying] is making you ill."

Slater hoped the course would open up a career in healthcare, but it's made no difference.

The 56-year-old considered moving away from Taranaki, but couldn't afford the costs of moving.

"You have to get your first aid course renewed, your annual practising certificate and I couldn't get a student allowance, so my student loan is quite big.

"You have to run a household and [try] to survive."

For Taranaki woman Sam Hoogeboom, Shelley's situation was all too familiar.

After graduating in 2024, she said she wasn't offered a job until 2025 at Taranaki Base Hospital, a 12-month maternity cover.

"Roughly, in my cohort, there was 24, and there was only me and another girl who got a position on Ward 2A. There were four who got jobs in the psych ward.

"Everyone else didn't get a position."

After her contract finished, Hoogeboom found work as an enrolled nurse at a general practice in Hāwera, but before that, she faced the realities of an understaffed health system.

"I was only a new grad, only three months in, and I was thrown onto a night shift, where you're getting 12 patients.

"When I was working as a healthcare assistant, even though I'm qualified as an EN, I was always being asked, 'Can you do blood sugars, can you do obs?'"

Glenda Houston, a member of the nurse's union's enrolled nurses section, said it didn't make sense why EN's were struggling to find work.

"It's just gut-wrenching, because we've got all these new grad nurses, who are full of enthusiasm and just want to do it, but they're just going on to do other work, because we can't get them jobs, and it's just not fair."

Houston said the nurses' union met with Health Minister Simeon Brown last December and sent a follow-up letter in February.

They asked for Health NZ to roll out an updated enrolled nurse scope of practise, a targeted workforce plan and to better utilise ENs.

This year, 106 graduate ENs accepted offers through Health NZ's graduate nursing portal, but Houston told Checkpoint enrolled nurses still felt neglected.

"We cover the shortfall. There's so much we can do, but they're not using us to our full potential.

"We are absolutely being underutilised, because we can bridge the gap in all sectors."

National chief nurse Nadine Gray told Checkpoint Health NZ was reviewing models of care and clinical practice protocols to help encourage EN employment.

World.title: International student attacked in Auckland now facing deportation
World.content:
An international student who was brutally attacked in an aggravated robbery in Auckland is now facing deportation amid attempts to resolve a series of visa and legal issues.

Gurleen Bahia, a 22-year-old from the Indian state of Punjab, was attacked last month in a Manukau car park.

Bahia came to New Zealand in 2024 to pursue a Level 5 Diploma in Ageing and Disability Services.

After completing the course, he decided to continue his studies and enrolled in a Level 7 Diploma in Community Healthcare and Support.

However, he missed several classes due to some family issues and was unable to complete the course.

Bahia tried but failed to extend his visa in April before applying for a new student visa in June, with Immigration New Zealand again rejecting the application.

Gurleen Bahia was stabbed in the finger and repeatedly struck on the head with the handle of a knife during the attack. RNZ / Blessen Tom

He is now fighting a deportation decision while recovering from injuries sustained in the Manukau attack.

Rob Cleary, acting detective senior sergeant at Counties Manukau Central CIB, said police were continuing to investigate an aggravated robbery at a Manukau car park on 19 October.

Cleary said Bahia had been parked in a car park off Manukau Station Road when he was approached by a person asking for money.

"This person returned a short time later with a group of people," he said.

"One person in this group made demands for money, threatening the victim before assaulting him."

Bahia said one of the individuals stabbed him in the finger and repeatedly hit him on the head with the handle of a knife.

The group also stole some of his belongings, including his phone, wallet and passport.

Police took Bahia to Middlemore Hospital, where he underwent surgery on his finger.

Police took Gurleen Bahia to Middlemore Hospital after the attack, where he underwent surgery on his injured finger. Supplied

The timing of the attack could not have been worse.

"I was already dealing with a lot of problems with my visa and was unfortunately involved in a court case as well," Bahia said.

Bahia faces five charges of theft after a flat mate allegedly used his car to steal petrol on multiple occasions in August.

Months later, Bahia received a court summons for five charges of theft.

"I didn't know what she had done and was completely unaware of all this," he said.

"I was living with this person, and it happened without my knowledge. I always paid for my own fuel. It was a huge surprise to me, too."

Bahia said the same individual had also stolen his laptop and phone and blocked him, leaving him unable to contact her.

The theft charges are ongoing.

Earlier this month, while Bahia was in court as part of the theft charges, Immigration Compliance served him with a deportation order.

"I'm in a very difficult situation. A lot of things have happened to me, and I don't really know what to do," he said.

He is due to appear in court again on 15 December.

Bahia said his treatment was ongoing and he was still unable to walk or stand for long periods.

"I've been told to rest for four weeks, and the wires and screws need to be removed after eight weeks," he said.

"It has already been four weeks since my surgery, so I need to stay here for another four weeks."

Jagdeep Singh Sidhu is an immigration adviser and president of NZ Forum for Immigration Professionals. Supplied

Jagjeet Singh Sidhu, an immigration adviser with more than 15 years of experience, has filed an application to have Bahia's deportation order cancelled.

Sidhu said Bahia had no family in New Zealand to support him and wanted to fight the deportation so he could complete his studies and continue receiving medical treatment.

"He's getting support from the local gurdwara, where he's getting food and he's staying with his friends, where he's not paying rent," he said.

Sidhu said it was unfortunate that all of this had happened to Bahia and they were doing their best to resolve his visa situation.

Mathew Harrington, an immigration lawyer with Queen City Law, said Bahia's options were now very limited.

"I think the key thing here is just ensuring that quality information is actually put in front of the decision maker," Harrington said.

He said there were no visa categories specifically for victims of crime, but the immigration system had various points where discretion could be exercised and special personal circumstances considered.

Mathew Harrington is an immigration lawyer at Queen City Law. Supplied

Harrington said the first step for Bahia should be to deal with the deportation order.

"It is absolute discretion," he said.

"But I think, given the facts involved here, you'd like to think that they're able to do something for him.

"And that might look like at the very first step, cancel that order, but then granting a visa of some type is a bit of a soft landing."

However, Harrington said the options for people in situations like Bahia's were limited.

"It's incredibly limited," he said.

"You could potentially go and approach the minister and seek intervention."

Cleary told RNZ police that enquiries into the aggravated robbery were ongoing.

"Later that day [October 19] units did locate a vehicle of interest to police," he said.

"Occupants of this vehicle were stopped and spoken to as part of enquiries. However, there was insufficient evidence to make an arrest."

Steve Watson, Immigration Compliance and Investigations general manager at Immigration New Zealand said all relevant information would be considered as part of the deportation decision-making process, including any request to cancel Bahia's deportation order.

"[Immigration New Zealand] will await the outcome of Mr Bahia's criminal proceedings before decisions are made regarding his deportation from New Zealand," he said.

For Bahia, finishing his studies remains his biggest priority.

"I want to finish my studies," he said.

World.title: New Palmerston North fire truck unable to be used due to 'electrical fault'
World.content:
Audio player for " New Palmerston North fire truck sitting idle " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._v0.KrRTFtoPsaA8nSDloPZ4KejQJr59ANQpD9ULgGwzaM0/emergencies_national/2711721%2Fnew-palmerston-north-fire-truck-unable-to-be-used-due-to-electrical-fault

New Palmerston North fire truck sitting idle Checkpoint Download MP3 4m

One of Fire and Emergency NZ's newest fire trucks is sitting idle at the Palmerston North fire station because of a problem with a roof-mounted monitor, just weeks after it entered service.

Another new fire truck, sent to the city a fortnight ago, was out of action last week when its exhaust fell off - one of several instances of this around the country.

A senior firefighter said having the trucks off the road could affect the response to big blazes, but Fire and Emergency said communities could be assured it would still rush to emergencies when needed.

'The exhaust fell off'

One of the two new MAN type 3 trucks sent to Palmerston North - bought back in 2019 - encountered a problem soon after arriving.

"It's only been on the run - in service - for about a week and half before it was coming back from a fire call and the exhaust fell off in traffic," said NZ Professional Firefighters Union Palmerston North branch president, senior station officer Tony Sealey.

"The truck that it replaced was meant to be going to Tauranga and they're now having to wait because we had to steal the exhaust of that MAN truck to keep this one on the run."

Sealey said the truck was out of action for half a day. A Fire and Emergency spokesperson said it was 90 minutes.

The spokesperson confirmed the same problem had happened in Wellington and Whanganui.

Sealey said the cause of the fault, which happened in a "small number" of the trucks, wasn't known.

"It's not being addressed. If this happens on an Auckland motorway or something like that, and an exhaust comes off at 100kmh, something bad might happen.

"We were just lucky it happened to be at 30kmh an hour coming back from a fire call, not going to it."

While that truck was back in operation, the other new one sent to the city, based at the Milson station, was not, due to an electrical fault in a monitor.

It was now sitting idle in the Palmerston North station.

"This one has been off the run now twice with separate issues, but this is the latest one, where the monitor is failing to work due to an electrical fault," Sealey said.

He wasn't sure how long that would take to fix. Mechanics were seeing if they could solve the problem with the wiring.

The Fire and Emergency spokesperson confirmed this.

"We are investigating the cause of these incidents and, as a precaution, are inspecting the other Angloco MAN type 3 appliances in the fleet."

Tony Searley says having one of the new trucks out of action could affect the response to large blazes. RNZ/Jimmy Ellingham

Fault affects responses - senior firefighter

Sealey feared losing one of Palmerston North's trucks could have a negative impact on the response to a large fire.

"We need to call back staff to assist in the larger-scale jobs. We now don't have a truck for them to ride, so we'll be calling in volunteers from out of district," he said.

"We won't have the resources on the fire ground to do, realistically, what we need to do, and in time.

"Where we would probably have extra resources within about 15-20 minutes, we're probably looking more at about half an hour to have the resources that we need, which when fire doubles in size every 30 seconds is a big deal."

The Fire and Emergency spokesperson said it had one of the largest fleets of commercial vehicles in New Zealand, about 1300 fire trucks and specialist response vehicles.

"We maintain the fleet to a high standard and service them regularly. These are large and complex appliances, and they are expected to have mechanical issues from time to time.

"We have a relief fleet to support such events and ensure there is no reduction in current response capability for the community," the spokesperson said.

"During incidents, our dispatching procedures enable us to call out the next available truck if the nearest truck is attending another call or is unavailable for any other reason, like scheduled maintenance or repair work.

"Communities can be assured Fire and Emergency will respond to emergencies when needed with the right resources."

Sealey, a firefighter of 23 years, said he had seen problems with vehicles being off the road and fleets not being upgraded for about 15 years.

MP concerned by problems

Fire and Emergency has faced heavy criticism over the purchase of the MAN type 3 trucks in 2019, as well as how long it's taken to roll them out.

RNZ has also previously reported they had problems fitting the essential lifesaving gear they need to carry.

National MP Tim Costley has questioned Fire and Emergency's top brass at select committee hearings and he wasn't surprised to hear about the latest problems.

"The high-pressure delivery unit we've known about for some time. I think part of this seems to come down to issues during the build, it comes down to a lack of specification during the design phase, and a lack of understanding in terms of the logic behind it."

It was good to see some of the MAN type 3 trucks in action, although the faults were concerning.

"Anything that goes wrong on a truck is a concern to me. I want our firefighters to be able to support our community and have the best possible support available.

"The issues that we're seeing really just point to the deeper issues that we've already identified that we know that we need to fix."

Costley said he looked forward to doing that should, as expected, National form part of a coalition government after special votes were counted.

Sealey would also like to see a fix.

"That is the frustrating thing for all the career firefighters. We just want to be able to turn up and do our jobs and have reliable equipment to help everyone that we need to help."

Fire and Emergency spent millions of dollars shipping 28 MAN type 3 trucks to Britain for their fitouts. Their total cost, including this, was $28.36 million, according to figures released under the Official Information Act.

World.title: Latest bridge proposal designed to spark public debate over second Auckland harbour crossing
World.content:
Promoters of the latest Auckland harbour crossing hope their proposed bridge project will spark public participation in the debate.

The plan features a new bridge running adjacent to the current structure, providing two rail lanes, and pedestrian and cycle access.

Great Auckland director Patrick Reynolds told RNZ Checkpoint that the design would prove cheaper and more attractive than the current tunnel preference.

"It would be beautiful, absolutely stunning, and would grace our glorious harbour and city, and would be an attraction in its own right." Reynolds said.

Audio player for " Advocacy group call for support on harbour crossing design " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._v0.KrRTFtoPsaA8nSDloPZ4KejQJr59ANQpD9ULgGwzaM0/regions/2711455%2Flatest-bridge-proposal-designed-to-spark-public-debate-over-second-auckland-harbour-crossing

Advocacy group call for support on harbour crossing design Checkpoint Download MP3 5m

"It would be something people could access to get right out on the harbour and we are dealing with some design input suggesting we can move down the walking path to the bottom of the piers, where there would be mussel beds and full engagement with the glorious Waitematā Harbour."

When complete, it would complement the existing bridge, which would carry traffic northbound, while the new bridge handles southbound flow.

"It's not immediately adjacent," he said. "It's quite a bit distant and goes from the existing viaduct, 30 metres above Westhaven Marina and flies to the old toll plaza.

The new bridge would ultimately carry southbound traffic, while the existing structure would handle the flow north. Nicolas Reid/MRCagney

"It doesn't touch Northcote Point, where the current bridge does. It very gently connects at each end - that's the traffic portion."

Reynolds suggested - like the old bridge, which opened in 1959 - the new one could be built largely offsite and assembled on the harbour.

Once in place, it could handle traffic in both directions, while the existing structure was upgraded.

Although original costings had the project at $5-6 billion, Reynolds revealed latest estimates had halved that figure to about $2.6b.

"Bridges are always cheaper than tunnels," he said. "Tunnelling is a very complicated and difficult business, as Aucklanders are very familiar with, after CRL [City Rail Link], and the idea that tunnelling isn't disruptive is untrue."

Reynolds also hoped the proposal would encourage Aucklanders to be more involved in the decision process.

"We've got a petition and we really want a full conversation, so when a decision is made on the project, it has public support and they're fully informed - unlike the Auckland rail project, which was done in secret and dumped on us, and people weren't carried along.

"We need a better process that survives political changes, if we're going to do this.

World.title: Cricketers' association slams 'disgraceful' treatment of Sandpapergate players
World.content:
The CEO of the Australian Cricketers' Association, Paul Marsh, has labelled the media treatment of Australian Test players as "absolutely disgraceful".

Marsh has criticised the media coverage of players linked to the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal which has seen media teams taking videos and photos outside players' houses, most notably of Australia's Test captain, Pat Cummins.

"We've got media camped outside and hounding players' families in their private homes and with their personal activities and it's disgraceful in my view," Marsh told ABC Sport.

"This has been an issue where people's integrity's being questioned, left, right and centre."

The union leader has called for the media companies to consider their actions

"There's a human toll to this that I think is being disregarded in a lot of quarters," he said.

"The scrutiny, the accusations, the fact their families are being hounded here, like, this is really difficult.

"I'm really concerned about the players' well-being at the moment as a collective.

"The reality of this is, this is hurting I think everyone that's involved."

Steve Smith says he did not want to speak to the press on his return to the New South Wales set-up ahead of Sunday's Shield game. (Supplied: Channel 10)

Questions around who knew details of the 2018 Cape Town sandpaper plot have blown up in the past two weeks since the publication of Usman Khawaja's memoir, and a newspaper article by the player at the centre of the scandal, Cameron Bancroft.

Bancroft said that the entire 2018 team knew about the sandpaper plot.

Those allegations directly contradict other Australian players who played in the 2018 tour including Cummins, who held an extensive media conference denying any knowledge of the sandpaper plot.

Marsh is calling for space and perspective.

"Understandably people want to understand that the black and white of what might have happened here but I'm just not convinced we're going to get to that," he said.

"What I do think we need to do is find a way to get the players and others that were involved together and talk about this and actually try to find a way through.

"I do think that they might need everyone here to give a bit."

Pat Cummins spoke in front of a press conference for 68 minutes, but has also been door-stopped outside his home. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

He said mistakes were made by all parties in 2018 that are adding to the current febrile environment.

"I think there was a lot of pressure put on the team at the time from Cricket Australia, and I think they need to take some responsibility," Marsh said.

"I think time again, maybe the whole playing group should have taken a collective responsibility for this, whether they knew or they didn't know.

"I think that also needs to be an understanding that one person's recollection of what happened here, might be different to somebody else's — [that] doesn't mean that anyone's not telling the truth."

Cricket Australia (CA) this week announced the formation of a forum to allow players to discuss their recollection of events in 2018 behind closed doors.

But the proposal has been criticised because it won't take the form of an inquiry to find a set of agreed facts and because the CA board will decide what it will and won't release after the forum is completed.

CA hasn't released the terms of reference for the forum, nor has it named a person to oversee it.

Marsh said while he was supporting the attempt to find a way to move forward, he said he was still waiting on the details of the forum.

Steve Smith has not made any comments since the release of Usman Khawaja's book, Sabr. (Supplied: Channel 10)

"I'd probably rather understand exactly what they're proposing before I get into assessing it," he said.

He said the Australian players want what's best for Australian cricket.

"Let's work out how we can get there because if we don't do that, I feel like we're going to stay in the place that we're at the moment, which is hurting everyone," he added.

He said while he accepted the public want to know who knew what regarding the sandpaper plot, that may be impossible.

"I think we all would love to have a, you know, an accepted set of facts, but the reality of this is we don't," he said.

"I've had lots of conversations with players the last two weeks, and you know, players with no reason to tell me any differently than what is the truth.

"Players are saying, 'I don't remember the meeting that's been referred to here' or the next person saying, 'I think we had that meeting', and this is what we're dealing with at the moment.

"I would just ask consider the human element of what these guys are going through at the moment."

World.title: AFLW physicality helps resilient Tayla Harris 'feel alive'
World.content:
Tayla Harris has always been a player for the big moments.

The Melbourne forward is renowned for high-flying marks and picture-perfect kicks.

But with Melbourne down by seven points in the fourth quarter of its qualifying final against Geelong, it was Harris's grit that delivered.

Harris, knowing how ex-Melbourne coach Mick Stinear talks about the inside and outside layers of a contest, realised Cats star Nina Morrison would win the ball in the latter.

She made her move, flattening Morrison with a perfectly timed, legal and brutal bump.

It set the tone as Tom Wilson's Melbourne completed a turnaround from 28 points down to beat Geelong and reach Saturday's preliminary final against Carlton at Princes Park.

"That's how I play," Harris said.

Tayla Harris's physicality isn't always reflected in the stats. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Martin Keep)

"I would like to think that people know that I only ever play with fair intent.

"And our game requires some pretty impactful moments.

"And I'll cop it back, no problem — and I do often. A few Geelong players got me good.

"Hell yeah, this is how I feel alive."

Harris, 29, knows her impact goes beyond the stat sheet.

"What I do with my physicality and presence I know has an impact on our team in a positive way, so I'll continue to do whatever's required in that moment," she said.

"If it's putting your body on the line, if it's spoiling or if it's running hard, whatever it might require, all of us would agree that, particularly in finals, those little moments matter."

Two years ago, bumping and clunking overhead marks appeared a pipe dream.

Tayla Harris struggled with injuries to her shoulders 12 months ago. (Getty Images: Kelly Defina)

The ruck-forward had surgery on her loose shoulders, one after the other, but never doubted she would return.

"I'm pretty determined when it comes to overcoming adversity or being told that I can't," Harris said.

"I'm pretty bullish on proving to myself that I can."

Having dealt with two trades, plus a failed trade to Hawthorn and a rise to fame and highly publicised social media abuse, there is not much Harris can not handle.

"My career hasn't been one that's been straightforward and all roses, which I'm really thankful for because it builds resilience," Harris said.

"And the adversity that I have faced has made me a better player, but more importantly, person.

"When it was hitting the fan, it's all happening. And then you feel like the world's collapsing in and then next minute it's all good again. But that's life."

Harris practises breathwork and maintains her boxing fitness, a throwback to a childhood that juggled football with waterskiing and skateboarding.

"I'd spend hours on the street trying to do a kickflip, and I'd fail 100 times, and then I would maybe get one and think that I was Tony Hawk," she said.

"I'm so glad that I grew up that way and with my parents not letting me believe that failure was a bad thing — it was just part of it.

"The only way that you're ever going to get anywhere is to fail.

"One thing I know for sure is I will continue to get it wrong and continue to make mistakes and continue to fail, so to speak, but that's the only way I'll ever keep growing or get better."

Inaugural AFLW star Harris would love to play for several more years.

But first, the 2022 premiership winner wants another flag.

"We believe we can go all the way. But we are absolutely set on this next game that we have," Harris said.

"We recently watched a Kobe Bryant press conference and they'd gone up 2-0 in the playoffs and the journalist had said 'why aren't you smiling?'

"And he's got a straight face and goes, 'Job's not done.'

"So that's our philosophy at the moment and we're certainly not looking ahead. But we certainly believe."

AAP

World.title: Media locked out of Steve Smith training session at SCG
World.content:
Steve Smith has returned to training in a covert session with New South Wales as the hierarchy closes ranks around Australia's star batsman.

Smith arrived at the Sydney Cricket Ground today through a back entrance, and media were locked out of watching the ex-Test captain bat in the nets.

The 37-year-old has maintained his silence amid a fresh furore surrounding the sandpaper scandal.

After returning from New York earlier this week, Smith is expected to play for the Blues in their Sheffield Shield game against Queensland at the SCG starting on Sunday.

Smith has not played any cricket since suffering a neck injury in the second Test on last month's tour of South Africa.

Current Test captain Pat Cummins and his national cohorts Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon also could feature in the NSW side in the final round of Shield games before Australia name a squad for the first Test against New Zealand starting December 9.

Those four bowlers did not attend Blues training yesterday.

Smith has not spoken publicly since the release of Usman Khawaja's autobiography, which has triggered an unheralded split in Australian cricket.

Khawaja wrote that all players were aware of Australia's ball tampering in the infamous Test match against South Africa in 2018.

That version was rejected as nonsense by Cummins, but has been supported by David Warner, Cameron Bancroft and Chadd Sayers.

Cummins bluntly denied any knowledge of Australia using sandpaper on the ball in Cape Town.

But Bancroft, in a written account issued on Wednesday night, said all players knew the plan.

Smith, Test skipper at the time, was banned by Cricket Australia for 12 months and stripped of the captaincy.

Warner was also suspended for a year and removed from the vice-captaincy, while Bancroft, who was caught by television cameras in Cape Town with sandpaper, was banned for nine months.

AAP

World.title: F1 is in Las Vegas, and teams are fighting to hit prize money jackpot
World.content:
Kimi Antonelli has won the F1 drivers' championship, his Mercedes team is constructors' champion, and there are just three rounds left in the season.

But the final trio of grand prix, starting this Sunday (AEDT) in Las Vegas, are not just for show.

These three races, for every team other than Mercedes, are the most important three weekends of the 2026 season.

Why? It's all about the money.

While fans mostly focus on the drivers' championship, it is the constructors' championship that carries the most significance for teams.

The prize money handed out at the end of the year is tied to where you finish in the team's championship. The higher you finish, the more money you receive.

While the exact figure each season is not made public, UK outlet The Independent published a rough guide to potential earnings this season, based of figures gathered from 2025.

Potential F1 2026 prize money *as per The Independent, all figures are in USD 1st — $140m 2nd — $131m 3rd — $122m 4th — $113m 5th — $104m 6th — $95m 7th — $87m 8th — $78m 9th — $69m 10th — $60m 11th — $51m

As the champion, Mercedes is expected to be awarded about $US140 million ($208 million).

But the other 10 teams in this year's championship have not solidified their spot in the championship, meaning there is plenty to race for in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

There is a maximum of 129 points a team can win to finish the season; they would need their drivers to finish first and second in all three grand prix.

Ferrari currently sits in second place with 510 points, 95 ahead of Red Bull. The Scuderia just need 34 more points from the final three races to be certain of second place.

But the battle for third between Red Bull and McLaren should be a belter.

Red Bull sits on 415 points, led by superstar Max Verstappen, who sits second in the drivers' championship with 279 points to his name.

Red Bull sits just 17 points ahead of McLaren, which has been an up-and-down season for drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

The difference between third and fourth this season appears to be worth roughly $US9 million ($13.3 million), and every point will be crucial.

F1 constructors' standings before Las Vegas 1: 652 — Mercedes CHAMPION 2: 512 — Ferrari 3: 415 — Red Bull 4: 398 — McLaren 5: 112 — Racing Bulls 6: 69 — Alpine 7: 31 — Haas 8: 28 — Audi 9: 12 — Williams 10: 7 — Aston Martin 11: 0 — Cadillac

"We'll do our best to make sure it goes down to the wire and in our favour," McLaren race director Randy Singh told the F1 Nation podcast this week about his team's battle with Red Bull.

"We're treating it like a mini championship on our side, so we're just aiming to do our best at each race."

Racing Bulls appears all but set to place fifth, and Alpine looks to be safe in sixth, with any team below them needing to increase their season tally by more than double just to match them before this weekend's action.

The final five teams in the championship: Haas (31), Audi (28), Williams (12), Aston Martin (7) and Cadillac (0) are separated by just 31 points.

Haas and Audi are separated by just three points with three rounds to go, while Williams and Aston Martin are separated by just five.

If either of these teams can secure a remarkable and unlikely podium placing in the final three races, they will almost certainly leapfrog at least one rival and bag themselves a few extra million dollars.

F1 to have full-time stewards from 2027

Formula 1 will have full-time stewards from next season in a bid to create greater consistency in officiating.

Stewards play a crucial, and at times defining, role in races, as they are in charge of regulating rule breaches and handing out penalties.

Until now, stewards for F1 races have been selected from a pool on a race-by-race basis.

But with the demand for greater consistency in how rules are enforced and penalties handed down, a full-time group will be introduced.

It is expected that a team of 12-15 stewards will make up the team, with a smaller pool starting next season, supported by members of the current stewards pool used.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula 1 World Championship; it is also an investment in the future of our sport," FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said.

F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix start time

Here is when the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix begins in your state or territory.

3pm AEDT: NSW, Victoria, ACT, Tasmania

2:30pm: ACDT: South Australia

2pm AEST: Queensland

12pm AWST: Western Australia

ABC Sport will have a live blog of the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix from 1pm AEDT on Sunday, November 22.

World.title: NRL and NRLW 2027 draw released, with lengthy wait for grand final rematch
World.content:
The NRL will introduce a Super Sunday to accommodate Perth's entry in the 2027 season, with an extra game added to the end of each weekend as part of an 18-team competition.

League officials revealed the draw for next year on Friday, with Parramatta and the Gold Coast to kick off the season in Las Vegas alongside Melbourne and Wests Tigers.

The Dolphins, North Queensland and South Sydney have emerged as the biggest winners, while Melbourne and Brisbane have been served two of the most difficult schedules.

NRL round one, 2027 Sunday, February 28 Parramatta Eels vs Gold Coast Titans, Las Vegas

Melbourne Storm vs Wests Tigers, Las Vegas Thursday, March 4 Sydney Roosters vs Brisbane Broncos, Sydney Football Stadium Friday, March 5 New Zealand Warriors vs Canterbury Bulldogs, Mt Smart Stadium

St George Illawarra Dragons vs North Queensland Cowboys, Jubilee Stadium Saturday, March 6 Dolphins vs Cronulla Sharks, Dolphin Stadium

Newcastle Knights vs Penrith Panthers, Hunter Stadium Sunday, March 7 Perth Bears vs Manly Warringah Sea Eagles, Perth Stadium

Canberra Raiders vs South Sydney Rabbitohs, Canberra Stadium

Under the newly constructed draw, no team will have more than one five-day turnaround, with 16 of them shared evenly across the league.

The vast majority of weekends will consist of one game on a Thursday night, two on a Friday and then three on both a Saturday and Sunday.

The NRL had previously steered away from a 2pm Sunday time slot early in the season due to hot weather, but that is no longer possible in the new fixture.

Sunday night games will also be a constant across the majority of the year, with the Bears hosting five of those to ensure more daytime football due to the west coast time difference.

Newcastle will have to wait until round 10 to try to exact revenge on the Sydney Roosters for last year's grand final, with a rematch set for Saturday, May 8.

That is the longest wait for a grand-final rematch since Canberra and the Roosters in the COVID-hit 2020 draw.

The Roosters will have a number of grudge matches locked in before the Knights clash, given they face Brisbane in the opening round and arch-rivals South Sydney in round two.

Payne Haas could feel the wrath of a Lang Park crowd for three straight weeks in 2027, with the ex-Bronco able to set up camp in Brisbane for the month of May.

South Sydney recruit Haas is set to travel to Lang Park to meet Brisbane for the first time in round 10.

After coming up against the Broncos on Thursday, May 6, South Sydney will then face North Queensland at Lang Park the following Sunday for Magic Round.

Assuming Haas is then picked for NSW in State of Origin, he will then feature in the series opener at the same ground on May 26 for the Blues.

Wests Tigers will have to wait only four weeks to take on their former halfback Jarome Luai, after his exit for Parramatta for next season.

Luai's signing with the PNG Chiefs for 2028 derailed the Tigers' season before he was released from his contract a year early to head to the Eels.

The NRLW draw was also released on Friday, with the competition having a trio of prime-time Thursday night matches.

Reigning premiers Sydney will host Wests Tigers to open the season on Thursday, July 1.

St George Illawarra will host Parramatta in round 10, while the Gold Coast hosts Brisbane in round 11 in the other two Thursday night clashes.

AAP/ABC

World.title: Young Aussies stun Argentina at under-17 World Cup
World.content:
Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon has demonstrated why he's one of the most exciting talents in Australian football as he inspired the Joeys to a shock 2–0 victory over Argentina to launch their U17 World Cup campaign in style in Qatar.

The brilliant young winger had his shot deflected for an own goal on the hour and then produced an audaciously cheeky finish 11 minutes later to seal the opening-day win on Thursday (Friday AEDT) as Carl Veart's side provided a magnificent return to the global boys' competition for the first time in seven years.

Against one of the powerhouse soccer nations, Australia had their backs to the wall, having to make 31 clearances as Argentina enjoyed two-thirds of the possession and 22 shots on goal, but Akon ended up hailing their second-half heist as "amazing".

The 17-year-old livewire provided the real star quality, and it was soon evident why the Sky Blues had wanted to keep him back in Australia for their A-League Men campaign.

He caused havoc from the start down the right flank, his neat through ball in the fifth minute almost resulting in a goal for Central Coast Mariners' Luke Becvinovski.

Akon then struck after the break following another dangerous foray down the right flank that ended with his shot across goal deflecting off the hapless Alvaro Guich and into the net.

In the 71st minute, Mariners' Oli O'Carroll expertly picked off an Argentina attack before Brisbane's Emmett Shaw released Akon with a slide-rule left-foot pass, the winger going on to dummy the goalkeeper before slotting into an empty net.

It only got worse for Argentina when substitute Benjamin Vallejos got sent off for a reckless challenge in stoppage time.

But it wasn't all about Akon, a considerable talent who's already made his national U23 bow.

At the other end, Charlie Wilson-Papps, the young goalie who's on Premier League Brighton's books, made half-a-dozen fine saves and kept a clean sheet.

"I do it for my teammates. I do it for my family at home. So to make them proud is the most important thing," said Akon, as he clutched the player-of-the-match trophy afterwards.

His only worry came with the video checking of his goal. "Ah, that was nerve-racking, man. Because at 1-0, it was a very scary game. So to be able to seal it like that, the coach was telling me it was a goal.

"The first goal? It wasn't really my goal, but I just wanted to do the Tim Cahill, start off the tournament like that. So, yeah, the knee side had to come with it.

"Now, the group, we're really confident, really confident in our ability, and I think that showed today."

Next up on Sunday for the Joeys will be Denmark, who lost 4–0 to Mozambique in their group C opener on Thursday.

AAP

World.title: Football club wishes manager a happy birthday, then sacks him hours later
World.content:
English football club Blackpool has sacked manager Ian Evatt, just hours after the club wished him a happy birthday on its social media accounts.

Blackpool plays in League One, the third tier of English football, and is languishing in 20th position, with just three wins from 13 matches this season.

Evatt was an accomplished player for Blackpool during a successful seven-year stint, where the Tangerines rose from the third tier of English football to the Premier League.

On Thursday, the club posted on social media that morning, wishing Evatt a happy 45th birthday.

Seven hours later, the club posted on social media that he had been sacked.

On the left, Blackpool FC with coach Ian Evatt a happy birthday. On the right, the club announces his sacking on the same day. (X/BBC Sport)

Evatt took over the manager role in October, 2025, helping the struggling club avoid relegation.

But the club finds itself in another relegation battle this season.

"Blackpool Football Club can announce that Ian Evatt has departed his role as Head Coach after 12 months in charge," the club said in a statement.

"During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Ian made over 250 appearances for the Seasiders. In his six years at Blackpool, he played a vital role in the Club's memorable rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

"The Club thanks Ian for all of his efforts during his time at Bloomfield Road."

World.title: Paralympian local MP playing her third sport for Australia
World.content:
Politician, Paralympic gold medallist and Australian Para Ice Hockey player.

The unique description belongs to 57-year-old Liesl Tesch MP, who is balancing her role as the Gosford MP with the upcoming 2026 Para Ice Hockey Women's World Championships in Newcastle this month.

After seven Paralympic Games appearances across wheelchair basketball and sailing with a pair of gold medals, most would be more than content with their sporting careers, but Tesch wants more.

While sporting success has tended to follow Tesch wherever she has gone, getting used to it on the ice was not as immediate.

"The first day I felt like a turtle upside down," Tesch told ABC Sport.

"The next day, I was like, 'oh my God, how was I so bad,' [but] I have fallen in love with this sport.

"It just gives me such a rush, and it's [wild] and brutal and crazy."

Loading Instagram content

A second chance

The 2026 Para Ice Hockey Women's World Championships will be the second of its kind, with the inaugural event held in Slovakia last year. Australia competed, finishing sixth, and losing all three of their matches in Dolný Kubín without scoring.

Lynda Holt, 54, is Ice Hockey Australia’s head of para ice hockey and also a Paralympian, and says this time will be different.

"We've all grown in the last year, we've all improved so much, and we have got some new players," Holt told ABC Sport.

"The team is great. I come from a shot put and discus background, a very individual sport on my own, and I'm just loving that we are this team that comes together."

Lynda Holt was part of the team at last year's event. (Supplied: Igor Kupco)

Australia will be joined by Canada, the United States, Great Britain, Norway, and Team World, a combination of players from countries not represented.

The six teams will be split into two groups of three, with Australia in Group A alongside the United States and Great Britain.

The game is played on sleds, and like mainstream ice hockey, it is played six-a-side, with most rules carried over.

For Tesch, it is a much-needed opportunity for women to shine.

"It's a chance for women to get together and play against women because a lot of us, we are training and playing against the blokes," Tesch said.

Australia did not win a game at the last world championships, but they are ready for the challenge this time. (Supplied: Igor Kupco)

Road to the Paralympics

Like several of her teammates, Lynda Holt knows the pressure of competing at a Paralympic Games, and being a part of landmark moments.

A shot put silver medallist at Sydney 2000, she recognises a chance now to be involved in another one, with the sport hoping for Paralympic inclusion as a full women's competition as soon as 2030.

She is not alone. Decorated swimmer Priya Cooper, who won nine gold medals across four Paralympic Games appearances, will also take to the ice, along with Susan Seipel, who won a silver medal as a Para canoeist at the Tokyo Games.

Tesch and fellow Paralympic silver medallist in wheelchair basketball, Lisa Edmonds, have both medalled on the court, and want to be part of a movement for women's para ice hockey players to have the same chance.

The push is on to get a standalone event into the Winter Paralympics. (ABC Sport: Bridget Murphy)

Para Ice Hockey has officially been a mixed gender event since the 2010 Paralympic Games, but Norway's Britt Mjaasund Øyen competed in 1994 as part of the team that won silver.

She was the first of only four women to compete at the level. Fellow Norwegian Lena Schrøder competed in 2018 and will captain Norway at this World Championships.

While the opportunity is there for women to compete alongside men, Holt is part of a wider community wanting a standalone women's tournament, something the event in Newcastle could help provide.

"Our whole goal, our whole movement we have got going on is [that] we have got to get there," Holt said.

"In order to qualify for the Paralympics, we needed to have two World Championships; this will be the second.

"We also need eight teams; we currently have five, and we have got three in development, so come next year, when they decide if we can be part of the Paralympics, we should be ready.

"This is history in the making for us."

Lynda Holt was a shot put silver medallist at Sydney 2000. (Supplied: SE Photography/Shannen Keddie)

The fight for time on ice

Ice hockey's growth in popularity around Australia has meant ice time has been harder to come by, regardless of what discipline you are attempting to play.

The Hunter Ice Skating Stadium, where the team have been training, is also home to several teams belonging to the hometown Newcastle Northstars, including its stand-up men's team, who are the Australian Ice Hockey League's most successful, having won its seventh title earlier this year.

Members of the public are also able to access the space, something Leisl Tesch knows all too well.

"Getting on here with the general public, I remember the first day I did it," she said.

"Everyone's standing up looking beautiful, and I am in this full body armour, but it is really good for speed and turn training with everyone else.

"It is also an inclusion conversation that people with disabilities can get on the ice too."

Holt and Edmonds are both based in Sydney, having to make the trip to Newcastle to train.

Loading Instagram content

"There's not enough ice time for everyone, and it's such an expensive sport, six to seven hundred dollars an hour for the ice," Holt said.

"We're all fighting for it; we've all got goals, ours is the Paralympics."

The tournament starts on November 24, with Canada's clash against Team World. Australia will open its campaign the same day, against the United States.

This content was produced for the ABC’s International Day of People with Disability coverage, which runs from November 19 to December 10, 2026.

The ABC is partnering with International Day of People with Disability to recognise the contributions and achievements of the 5.5 million Australians with disability.

Tech.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

Apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps. It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities, as a report from Bloomberg suggests the company could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs. This lines up with the company’s new job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.

“People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.”

With its upcoming iOS 27.3 update, Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.

Tech.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
Tech.content:
is an independent reporter focused on business investigations, analysis and news. She previously covered the AI data center boom for Business Insider.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

“We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company’s third quarter earnings call.

By Thursday, the company’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected.

Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in company history,” Kress told investors.

“Our momentum is real,” Kress said. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.”

But investors are stilltrying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future.

The company’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The New York Times.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession plan — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on.

It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia.

On October 29th, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.”

Nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June.

The stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the new class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64.

Then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a company-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang said he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025.

The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee.

Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the company’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year.

On December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd.

Retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research.

They might be onto something.

Nvidia’s average price target is $232.59, with the lowest estimate at $130 and the highest at $350, according to an analysis of analyst projections over the last three months by Google Finance.

Nearly two-thirds of those analysts issued a “Buy” rating for Nvidia in the last three months. Of those, all 30 reiterated that rating post-earnings.

The stock closed at $145.98 on Thursday, a new 52-week low.

Then again, numbers are the core basis for stock market ratings, and numbers may not be Nvidia’s problem right now. It’s everything else — the leadership vacuum, upcoming congressional testimony, regulatory uncertainty, broader questions about neocloud customer financing and sales to China — that will continue to impact the stock in the coming weeks.

Tech.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
Tech.content:

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Meta is planning to price the Muse Charm, a little gadget with a screen that lets you chat with your Muse AI agent, at $300, according to The Information. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the gadget earlier this year and said the company expected to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but he didn’t provide a price at the time.

When he announced the Muse Charm, Zuckerberg said that the company had “packed the whole Muse experience,” including real-time voice and avatar technology, into the gadget. It has a fingerprint sensor, and you can tap it to be able to talk to a Muse AI agent without unlocking a phone or opening an app. The Information reports that the Muse Charm will come with a free 12-month 5G data plan from Verizon.

Spokesperson Tyler Yee wrote to The Information that “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.” When reached for comment by The Verge, Yee provided the same statement.

The company is also working on a smartwatch, The Information says, but a launch for that has been pushed to 2027 as Meta tries to get Muse Charm out the door.

Meta also open sourced code to let users make their own Muse gadgets, which my colleague Sean Hollister used to make his own DIY Muse Charm.

Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.
